title.zh: 卷四十一 列傳第一 后妃
title.raw: 卷四十一 列傳第一 后妃 Volume 41 Biographies 1: Emperesses and Consorts

sentences.zh: 帝祖母號太皇太后，母號皇太后，妃號皇后，漢舊制也。

translations.literal: The emperor's paternal grandmother was styled Grand Empress Dowager, his mother was styled Empress Dowager, and his consort was styled Empress — this was the old Han regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han precedent, the emperor's grandmother took the title Grand Empress Dowager, his mother Empress Dowager, and his principal consort Empress.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝採漢、魏之制，置貴嬪、夫人、貴人，是為三夫人，位視三公。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin adopted the systems of Han and Wei, establishing Honored Consort, Lady, and Honored Person; these were the Three Consorts, with rank equivalent to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin drew on Han and Wei precedent to establish the offices of Honored Consort, Lady, and Honored Person as the Three Consorts, each with rank on a par with the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 淑妃、淑媛、淑儀、脩華、脩容、脩儀、婕妤、容華、充華，是為九嬪，位視九卿。

translations.literal: Pure Consort, Pure Lady, Pure Ceremony, Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Countenance, Cultivated Ceremony, Talented Beauty, Splendid Countenance, and Fulfilling Splendor — these were the Nine Consorts, with rank equivalent to the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The nine ranks of Pure Consort, Pure Lady, Pure Ceremony, Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Countenance, Cultivated Ceremony, Talented Beauty, Splendid Countenance, and Fulfilling Splendor formed the Nine Consorts, each with rank equivalent to one of the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 其餘有美人、才人、中才人，爵視千石以下。

translations.literal: Besides these there were Beautiful Lady, Talented Lady, and Middle Talented Lady, with stipends equivalent to offices below one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Lower still were the Beautiful Lady, Talented Lady, and Middle Talented Lady, whose emoluments matched posts below the rank of one thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 高祖受命，省二才人，其餘仍用晉制。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor received the Mandate, he abolished the two Talented Lady posts; the rest still followed the Jin system.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, he eliminated the two Talented Lady offices but otherwise retained the Jin arrangements.

sentences.zh: 貴嬪，魏文帝所制。

translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort was an office created by Emperor Wen of Wei.

translations.idiomatic: Lady was instituted when Cao Cao first established the state of Wei.

translations.idiomatic: Honored Person was an office created by Emperor Guangwu of Han.

translations.idiomatic: Talented Beauty and Splendid Countenance were titles inherited from the Former Han.

sentences.zh: 充華，晉武帝所制。

translations.idiomatic: Fulfilling Splendor was an office created by Emperor Wu of Jin.

translations.idiomatic: Beautiful Lady was an office created by Emperor Guangwu of Han.

sentences.zh: 世祖孝建三年，省夫人、脩華、脩容，置貴妃，位比相國，進貴嬪，位比丞相，貴人位比三司，以為三夫人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian of Emperor Shizu, Lady, Cultivated Splendor, and Cultivated Countenance were abolished; Imperial Consort was established with rank equal to Chancellor of State; Honored Consort was promoted with rank equal to Chancellor; Honored Person with rank equal to the Three Dukes — these formed the Three Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xiaojian era, Emperor Xiaowu abolished the offices of Lady, Cultivated Splendor, and Cultivated Countenance, created Imperial Consort with rank matching the Chancellor of State, elevated Honored Consort to rank matching the Chancellor, and set Honored Person at rank matching the Three Dukes, thus reconstituting the Three Consorts.

sentences.zh: 又置昭儀、昭容、昭華，以代脩華、脩儀、脩容。

translations.literal: He also established Illustrious Ceremony, Illustrious Countenance, and Illustrious Splendor to replace Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Ceremony, and Cultivated Countenance.
translations.idiomatic: He further established Illustrious Ceremony, Illustrious Countenance, and Illustrious Splendor in place of Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Ceremony, and Cultivated Countenance.

sentences.zh: 又置中才人、充衣，以為散位。

translations.literal: He also established Middle Talented Lady and Fulfilling Attire as honorary posts.
translations.idiomatic: Middle Talented Lady and Fulfilling Attire were added as supplementary, non-ranked offices.

translations.idiomatic: Illustrious Ceremony was an office created by Emperor Yuan of Han.

translations.idiomatic: Middle Talented Lady was an office created by Emperor Wu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 太宗泰始元年，省淑妃、昭華、中才人、充衣，復置脩華、脩儀、脩容、才人、良人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taishi of Emperor Taizong, Pure Consort, Illustrious Splendor, Middle Talented Lady, and Fulfilling Attire were abolished; Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Ceremony, Cultivated Countenance, Talented Lady, and Good Lady were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taishi era, Emperor Ming abolished Pure Consort, Illustrious Splendor, Middle Talented Lady, and Fulfilling Attire, and restored Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Ceremony, Cultivated Countenance, Talented Lady, and Good Lady.

sentences.zh: 三年，又省貴人，置貴姬，以備三夫人之數。

translations.literal: In the third year he again abolished Honored Person and established Honored Concubine to complete the number of the Three Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he eliminated Honored Person and created Honored Concubine to fill out the complement of the Three Consorts.

sentences.zh: 又置昭華，增淑容、承徽、列榮。

translations.literal: He also restored Illustrious Splendor and added Pure Countenance, Bearing Insignia, and Arrayed Glory.
translations.idiomatic: Illustrious Splendor was reinstated, and the offices of Pure Countenance, Bearing Insignia, and Arrayed Glory were added.

sentences.zh: 以淑媛、淑儀、淑容、昭華、昭儀、昭容、脩華、脩儀、脩容為九嬪。

translations.literal: Pure Lady, Pure Ceremony, Pure Countenance, Illustrious Splendor, Illustrious Ceremony, Illustrious Countenance, Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Ceremony, and Cultivated Countenance were made the Nine Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Consorts now comprised Pure Lady, Pure Ceremony, Pure Countenance, Illustrious Splendor, Illustrious Ceremony, Illustrious Countenance, Cultivated Splendor, Cultivated Ceremony, and Cultivated Countenance.

sentences.zh: 婕妤、容華、充華、承徽、列榮凡五職，班亞九嬪。

translations.literal: Talented Beauty, Splendid Countenance, Fulfilling Splendor, Bearing Insignia, and Arrayed Glory — five offices in all — ranked below the Nine Consorts.
translations.idiomatic: Talented Beauty, Splendid Countenance, Fulfilling Splendor, Bearing Insignia, and Arrayed Glory formed a group of five offices ranking just below the Nine Consorts.

translations.literal: Beautiful Lady, Middle Talented Lady, and Talented Lady — three offices — served as miscellaneous attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Beautiful Lady, Middle Talented Lady, and Talented Lady were three supplementary attendant posts.

sentences.zh: 其後太宗留心後房，擬外百官，備位置內職。

translations.literal: Thereafter Emperor Taizong attended to the inner quarters, modeling the outer hundred officials and fully establishing inner offices.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Emperor Ming reorganized the inner palace, patterning its offices on the civil bureaucracy and filling out the ranks of the harem administration.

sentences.zh: 孝穆趙皇后諱安宗，下邳僮人也。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Xiaomu, née Zhao, personal name Anzong, was a native of Tong in Xiapi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Xiaomu Zhao, whose personal name was Anzong, came from Tong in Xiapi.

sentences.zh: 祖彪字世範，治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Biao, style Shifan, was Attendant Imperial Scribe for Legal Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Zhao Biao, styled Shifan, served as Attendant Imperial Scribe for Legal Documents.

sentences.zh: 父裔字彥冑，平原太守。

translations.literal: Her father Yi, style Yanzou, was Administrator of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zhao Yi, styled Yanzou, was Administrator of Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 永初二年，有司奏曰：「大孝之德，盛於榮親。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu, the relevant offices memorialized: "The virtue of supreme filial piety flourishes in honoring one's parents.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongchu, the responsible offices submitted a memorial: "The virtue of supreme filial piety reaches its height in honoring one's parents.

sentences.zh: 一人有慶，光被萬國。

translations.literal: When one person receives blessing, its light covers the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: When one person is blessed, that blessing shines upon all the realm.

sentences.zh: 是以靈文寵於西京，壽張顯於隆漢。

translations.literal: Therefore Lingwen was favored in the Western Capital, and Shouzhang was exalted in flourishing Han.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Lingwen was honored in the Western Capital, and Shouzhang was exalted in the flourishing Han.

sentences.zh: 故平原太守趙裔、故洮陽令蕭卓，並外屬尊戚，不逮休寵。

translations.literal: The late Administrator of Pingyuan Zhao Yi and the late Magistrate of Taoyang Xiao Zhuo were both honored relatives by marriage, yet had not received full rewards.
translations.idiomatic: The late Zhao Yi, Administrator of Pingyuan, and the late Xiao Zhuo, Magistrate of Taoyang, were both distinguished affinal kin, yet had not yet received the full honors due them.

sentences.zh: 臣等仰述聖思。

translations.literal: Your subjects respectfully set forth the sage intent.
translations.idiomatic: We, your subjects, respectfully follow Your Majesty's benevolent intent.

sentences.zh: 遠稽舊章，並可追贈光祿大夫，加金章紫綬。

translations.literal: Consulting distant precedents, both may posthumously be granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the golden seal and purple cord.
translations.idiomatic: Following ancient precedent, both should posthumously receive the title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, with the golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 裔命婦孫可豫章郡建昌縣君，卓命婦趙可吳郡壽昌縣君。」

translations.literal: Yi's wife Sun may be made Lady of Jianchang County in Yuzhang Commandery; Zhuo's wife Zhao may be made Lady of Shouchang County in Wu Commandery."
translations.idiomatic: Yi's wife Sun may be created Lady of Jianchang County in Yuzhang; Zhuo's wife Zhao may be created Lady of Shouchang County in Wu."

sentences.zh: 孫氏，東莞人也。

translations.literal: Sun was a native of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun was from Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 其年，又詔曰：「推恩之禮，在情所同。

translations.literal: That same year, another edict stated: "The rite of extending grace is what all hearts share alike.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, an edict further stated: "The rite of extending favor is one in which all share alike.

sentences.zh: 故內樹宗子，外崇后屬，爰自漢、魏，咸遵斯典。

translations.literal: Therefore within one establishes imperial sons, and without one honors the empress's kin — from Han and Wei onward, all have followed this canon.
translations.idiomatic: Within, one establishes the imperial sons; without, one honors the empress's kin — from Han and Wei onward, all have observed this rule.

sentences.zh: 外祖趙光祿、蕭光祿，名器雖隆，茅土未建，並宜追封開國縣侯，食邑五百戶。」

translations.literal: The maternal grandfathers Zhao the Grand Master and Xiao the Grand Master, though their titles were lofty, had received no fief; both should posthumously be enfeoffed as Marquises of a founding county with five hundred households."
translations.idiomatic: The maternal grandfathers, Zhao and Xiao, both Grandees of Splendid Happiness, though honored in title, had received no fief; both should posthumously be created Marquises of founding counties with five hundred households each."

sentences.zh: 於是追封裔臨賀縣侯。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yi was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Linhe County.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was then posthumously created Marquis of Linhe County.

sentences.zh: 裔長子宣之，仕至江乘令。

translations.literal: Yi's eldest son Xuanzhi rose to office as Magistrate of Jiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's eldest son Xuanzhi served as Magistrate of Jiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 蚤卒，無子，以弟孫襲之繼宣之紹封。

translations.literal: He died young without sons; his younger brother's grandson Xizhi succeeded Xuanzhi to inherit the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: He died young and left no son; his younger brother's grandson Xizhi succeeded him to inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 襲之卒，子祖憐嗣。

translations.literal: When Xizhi died, his son Zulian succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizhi died, his son Zulian succeeded.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，國除。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi accepted the abdication, the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 宣之弟倫之，自有傳。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi's younger brother Lunzhi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhi's younger brother Lunzhi has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 孝懿蕭皇后諱文壽，蘭陵蘭陵人也。

translations.literal: Empress Xiaoyi Xiao, personal name Wenshou, was a native of Lanling in Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xiaoyi Xiao, whose personal name was Wenshou, came from Lanling in Lanling Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖亮字保祚，侍御史。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Liang, style Baozuo, was Palace Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Xiao Liang, styled Baozuo, was Palace Censor.

sentences.zh: 父卓字子略，洮陽令。

translations.literal: Her father Zhuo, style Zilüe, was Magistrate of Taoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xiao Zhuo, styled Zilüe, was Magistrate of Taoyang.

sentences.zh: 孝穆后殂，孝皇帝娉后為繼室，生長沙景王道憐、臨川烈武王道規。

translations.literal: After Empress Dowager Xiaomu died, Emperor Xiaowu took the empress as his successor consort; she bore Prince Jing of Changsha Daolian and Prince Liewu of Linchuan Daogui.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Dowager Xiaomu's death, Emperor Xiaowu took her as his successor consort; she bore Prince Jing of Changsha, Daolian, and Prince Liewu of Linchuan, Daogui.

sentences.zh: 義熙七年，拜豫章公太夫人。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yixi she was invested as Grand Lady of the Duke of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of Yixi she received the title Grand Lady of the Duke of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 高祖為宋王，又加太妃之號。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor became Prince of Song, she was further given the title of Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu became Prince of Song, she was further styled Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 高祖以十二年北伐，仍停彭城、壽陽，至元熙二年入朝，因受晉禪，在外凡五年，后常留東府。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor on his northern campaign of the twelfth year remained at Pengcheng and Shouyang; he entered court in the second year of Yuanxi and thereupon received the Jin abdication — abroad altogether five years, while the empress usually remained at the Eastern Residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year Emperor Gaozu marched north and remained at Pengcheng and Shouyang; he entered court in the second year of Yuanxi and accepted the Jin abdication — away for five years in all, while the empress usually stayed at the Eastern Residence.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，有司奏曰：「臣聞道積者慶流，德洽者禮備。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor ascended the throne, the relevant offices memorialized: "Your subject has heard that where the Way accumulates, blessings flow forth; where virtue pervades, ritual is complete.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, the responsible offices memorialized: "We have heard that where the Way is amassed, blessings flow forth; where virtue is complete, ritual follows.

sentences.zh: 故祗敬表於崇高，嘉號彰於盛典。

translations.literal: Therefore reverent respect is displayed in loftiness, and fine titles shine forth in grand ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore reverence is shown in what is lofty, and honored titles are proclaimed in great ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 伏惟太妃母儀之德，化穆不言，保翼之訓，光被洪業。

translations.literal: We humbly consider that the Grand Consort's virtue as mother of the realm is serene in transforming influence and reticent in speech; her nurturing instruction has illumined the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly consider that the Grand Consort's virtue as mother of the realm is tranquil in its transforming power and modest in speech; her nurturing guidance has illuminated the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 雖幽明同慶，而稱謂未窮。

translations.literal: Though the hidden and manifest share in celebration, her titles have not yet been fully bestowed.
translations.idiomatic: Though the living and the dead share in rejoicing, her titles have not yet been fully bestowed.

sentences.zh: 稽之前代，禮有恒準，宜式遵舊章，允副羣望。

translations.literal: Examining former ages, ritual has constant standards; it is fitting to follow the old regulations and fulfill the hopes of all.
translations.idiomatic: Examining former ages, ritual has its constant standards; it is fitting to follow precedent and satisfy the hopes of all.

sentences.zh: 臣等請上宋王太后號皇太后。」

translations.literal: Your subjects request that the Prince of Song's mother be given the title Empress Dowager."
translations.idiomatic: We request that the Prince of Song's mother be given the title Empress Dowager."

sentences.zh: [2]故有司奏猶稱太妃也。

translations.literal: [2] Therefore in memorials the relevant offices still called her Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: [2] Accordingly, in memorials the offices still referred to her as Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 上以恭孝為行，奉太后素謹，及即大位，春秋已高，每旦入朝太后，未嘗失時刻。

translations.literal: The emperor took respectful filial piety as his conduct and served the empress dowager with constant care; after he took the great position, though already advanced in years, every morning he attended the empress dowager at court and never missed the hour.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made respectful filial piety his way of life and served the empress dowager with constant devotion; after his accession, though already advanced in years, every morning he attended her at court and never missed the appointed hour.

sentences.zh: 少帝即位，加崇曰太皇太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shaodi ascended the throne, she was further honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shaodi took the throne, she was further honored as Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 景平元年，崩于顯陽殿，時年八十一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingping she died in the Xianyang Hall, aged eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingping she died in the Xianyang Hall at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 遺令曰：「孝皇背世五十餘年，古不祔葬。

translations.literal: Her final testament stated: "Emperor Xiaowu has been gone more than fifty years; antiquity did not permit joint burial.
translations.idiomatic: Her testament read: "Emperor Xiaowu has been gone more than fifty years; antiquity did not permit joint burial.

sentences.zh: 且漢世帝后陵皆異處，今可於塋域之內別為一壙。

translations.literal: Moreover in Han times the tombs of emperors and empresses were all in separate places; now within the burial precinct a separate vault may be made.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in Han times imperial and empress tombs were always separate; within the burial precinct a separate vault may now be made.

sentences.zh: 孝皇陵墳本用素門之禮，與王者制度奢儉不同，婦人禮有所從，可一遵往式。」

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu's tomb originally followed the rites of a plain household, differing in extravagance and restraint from royal regulations; a woman's rites have what they follow — one may uniformly observe the former style."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu's tomb originally followed the rites of a common household, differing in splendor from royal regulations; a woman's rites have their own precedents — the former style may be followed throughout."

sentences.zh: 乃開別壙，與興寧陵合墳。

translations.literal: A separate vault was then opened and joined in burial mound with Xingning Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: A separate vault was opened and its burial mound joined with that of Xingning Tomb.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖微時，貧約過甚，孝皇之殂，葬禮多闕，高祖遺旨，太后百歲後不須祔葬。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Founding Emperor was in humble circumstances, poverty was extreme; at Emperor Xiaowu's death the funeral rites had many omissions, and the Founding Emperor left instructions that after the empress dowager reached a hundred years she need not be buried jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Gaozu was still obscure, poverty was extreme; at Emperor Xiaowu's death many funeral rites were omitted, and Gaozu left instructions that after the empress dowager reached a hundred years she need not receive joint burial.

sentences.zh: 至是故稱后遺旨施行。

translations.literal: Therefore it was said that the empress's testament was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it was said that the empress's testament was being followed.

sentences.zh: 卓初與趙裔俱贈金紫光祿大夫，又追封封陽縣侯，妻下邳趙氏封吳郡壽昌縣君。

translations.literal: Zhuo was at first together with Zhao Yi granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal, and was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Fengyang County; his wife Zhao of Xiapi was made Lady of Shouchang County in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo was at first, together with Zhao Yi, granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal, and was posthumously created Marquis of Fengyang County; his wife, Zhao of Xiapi, was made Lady of Shouchang County in Wu.

sentences.zh: 卓子源之襲爵，源之見子思話傳。

translations.literal: Zhuo's son Yuanzhi inherited the title; Yuanzhi's son Sihua has a biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuo's son Yuanzhi inherited the title; Yuanzhi's son Sihua has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 武敬臧皇后諱愛親，東莞人也。

translations.literal: Empress Wujing Zang, personal name Aiqin, was a native of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wujing Zang, whose personal name was Aiqin, came from Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 祖汪字山甫，尚書郎。

translations.literal: Her grandfather Wang, style Shanfu, was Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Zang Wang, styled Shanfu, was a Gentleman of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 父儁字宣乂，郡功曹。

translations.literal: Her father Jun, style Xuanyi, was Commandery Merit Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zang Jun, styled Xuanyi, was Commandery Merit Officer.

sentences.zh: 后適高祖，生會稽宣長公主興弟。

translations.literal: The empress married the Founding Emperor and bore the Princess Chang of Kuaiji, Xingdi.
translations.idiomatic: She married Emperor Gaozu and bore the Princess Chang of Kuaiji, Xingdi.

sentences.zh: 高祖以儉正率下，后恭謹不違。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor led his subordinates with frugal rectitude; the empress was respectful and careful and did not transgress.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu led his subordinates with frugal rectitude; the empress was respectful and careful and never transgressed.

sentences.zh: 及高祖興復晉室，居上相之重，而后器服粗素，不為親屬請謁。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor restored the Jin house and held the weight of chief minister, the empress's vessels and garments were coarse and plain, and she made no requests on behalf of kin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu restored the Jin house and held the weight of chief minister, the empress wore coarse and plain dress and made no requests on behalf of her kin.

sentences.zh: 義熙四年正月甲午，殂於東城，時年四十八，追贈豫章公夫人，還葬丹徒。

translations.literal: On the jiawu day of the first month of the fourth year of Yixi she died in the Eastern City, aged forty-eight; posthumously she was made Lady of the Duke of Yuzhang and was returned for burial in Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day of the first month of the fourth year of Yixi she died in the Eastern City at forty-eight; posthumously she was made Lady of the Duke of Yuzhang and was buried in Dantu.

sentences.zh: 高祖臨崩，遺詔留葬京師，於是備法駕，迎梓宮祔葬初寧陵。

translations.literal: At the Founding Emperor's deathbed his testament ordered burial in the capital; thereupon the imperial equipage was prepared and the coffin was welcomed for joint burial at Chuning Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: At Emperor Gaozu's deathbed his testament ordered burial in the capital; the imperial equipage was prepared and her coffin was welcomed for joint burial at Chuning Tomb.

sentences.zh: 宋初追贈儁金紫光祿大夫，妻高密叔孫氏封遷陵永平鄉君。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, Jun was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal; his wife Shusun of Gaomi was made Lady of Yongping Township in Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Song, Jun was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with golden seal; his wife, Shusun of Gaomi, was made Lady of Yongping Township in Qianling.

sentences.zh: [3]儁子燾，燾弟熹，熹子質，自有傳。

translations.literal: [3] Jun's son Yan, Yan's younger brother Xi, and Xi's son Zhi have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: [3] Jun's son Yan, Yan's younger brother Xi, and Xi's son Zhi have separate biographies.

sentences.zh: 武帝胡婕妤諱道安，[6]淮南人。

translations.literal: Honored Beauty Hu of Emperor Wu, personal name Dao'an,[6] was a native of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Beauty Hu of Emperor Wu, whose personal name was Dao'an,[6] came from Huainan.

sentences.zh: 義熙初，為高祖所納，生文帝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yixi she was taken in by the Founding Emperor and bore Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yixi she was taken in by Emperor Gaozu and bore Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 五年，被譴賜死，時年四十二。

translations.literal: In the fifth year she was condemned and granted death, aged forty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year she was condemned and ordered to take her own life at the age of forty-two.

sentences.zh: 葬丹徒。

translations.literal: She was buried in Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried in Dantu.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，追贈婕妤。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor ascended the throne, she was posthumously granted Honored Beauty.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu took the throne, she was posthumously granted the title Honored Beauty.

sentences.zh: 太后兄子元慶，位至奉朝請。

translations.literal: The empress dowager's nephew's son Yuanqing rose to the post of Court Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager's nephew's son Yuanqing rose to the post of Court Attendant.

sentences.zh: 文帝袁皇后諱齊媯，陳郡陽夏人，左光祿大夫敬公湛之庶女也。

translations.literal: Empress Yuan of Emperor Wen, personal name Qiji, was a native of Yangxia in Chen Commandery, a secondary daughter of Zuo Guanglu Dafu Jinggong Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yuan of Emperor Wen, whose personal name was Qiji, came from Yangxia in Chen Commandery; she was a secondary daughter of Left Director of the Masters of Writing for Splendid Happiness Jinggong Zhan.

sentences.zh: 母本卑賤，后年五六歲，方見舉。

translations.literal: Her mother was originally of humble status; only when the empress was five or six was she recognized and raised up.
translations.idiomatic: Her mother was originally of humble status; only when the empress was five or six was she recognized and raised in standing.

sentences.zh: 後適太祖，初拜宜都王妃。

translations.literal: Later she married Emperor Taizu and was at first invested as Princess of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: She later married Emperor Taizu and was at first invested as Princess of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 生子劭、東陽獻公主英娥。

translations.literal: She bore the son Shao and the Princess Xian of Dongyang, Ying'e.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Shao and the Princess Xian of Dongyang, Ying'e.

sentences.zh: 上待后恩禮甚篤，袁氏貧薄，后每就上求錢帛以贍與之，上性節儉，所得不過三五萬、三五十匹。

translations.literal: The emperor treated the empress with deep favor and courtesy; the Yuan clan was poor, and the empress often asked the emperor for money and cloth to support them; the emperor was by nature frugal, and what she received never exceeded thirty to fifty thousand cash or thirty to fifty bolts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated the empress with deep favor and courtesy; the Yuan clan was poor, and she often asked him for money and cloth to support them; he was by nature frugal, and what she received never exceeded thirty to fifty thousand cash or thirty to fifty bolts.

sentences.zh: 後潘淑妃有寵，愛傾後宮，咸言所求無不得，后聞之，欲知信否，乃因潘求三十萬錢與家，以觀上意，信宿便得。

translations.literal: Later Honored Consort Pan gained favor, and love in the inner palace inclined wholly to her; all said that what she sought was never denied. When the empress heard this, wishing to know whether it was true, she asked Pan for three hundred thousand cash for her family to observe the emperor's intent — within a day and night she received it.
translations.idiomatic: Later Honored Consort Pan gained favor, and the inner palace's affection inclined wholly to her; all said that what she sought was never denied. When the empress heard this, wishing to test the report, she asked Pan for three hundred thousand cash for her family to observe the emperor's intent — within a day and night she received it.

sentences.zh: 因此恚恨甚深，稱疾不復見上。

translations.literal: Because of this her resentment was very deep; she claimed illness and no longer saw the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this her resentment ran very deep; she claimed illness and would no longer see the emperor.

sentences.zh: 上每入，必他處回避。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor entered, she always avoided him elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor came in, she always avoided him elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 上數掩伺之，不能得。

translations.literal: The emperor several times concealed himself to watch for her but could not obtain a meeting.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor several times concealed himself to watch for her but could not obtain a meeting.

sentences.zh: 始興王濬諸庶子問訊，后未嘗視也。

translations.literal: When the various secondary sons such as Prince Jun of Shixing came to inquire after her health, the empress never looked at them.
translations.idiomatic: When the various secondary sons, including Prince Jun of Shixing, came to inquire after her health, the empress never even looked at them.

sentences.zh: 后遂憤恚成疾。

translations.literal: The empress thereupon fell ill from anger and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The empress thereupon fell ill from anger and resentment.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十七年，疾篤，上執手流涕問所欲言，[7]后視上良久，乃引被覆面。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia her illness was grave; the emperor held her hand with tears and asked what she wished to say;[7] the empress gazed at the emperor a long while, then drew up the coverlet over her face.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of Yuanjia her illness was grave; the emperor held her hand in tears and asked what she wished to say;[7] the empress gazed at him a long while, then drew the coverlet over her face.

sentences.zh: 崩于顯陽殿，時年三十六。

translations.literal: She died in the Xianyang Hall, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the Xianyang Hall at the age of thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 上甚相悼痛，詔前永嘉太守顏延之為哀策，文甚麗。

translations.literal: The emperor grieved deeply; he ordered the former Administrator of Yongjia Yan Yanzhi to compose a mourning text, and the writing was very beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply; he ordered the former Administrator of Yongjia Yan Yanzhi to compose a mourning text, and the prose was very beautiful.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its text reads:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: 龍輁纚綍，容翟結驂。

translations.literal: The dragon hearse with its trailing cords, pheasant banners and joined teams.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon hearse with trailing cords, pheasant banners, and paired teams.

sentences.zh: 皇塗昭列，神路幽嚴。

translations.literal: The imperial road shines in array; the spirit path is dark and solemn.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial road shines in array; the spirit path is dark and solemn.

sentences.zh: 皇帝親臨祖饋，躬瞻宵載。

translations.literal: The emperor in person came to the sending-off feast and himself gazed upon the night departure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in person attended the sending-off feast and himself gazed upon the night departure.

sentences.zh: 飾遺儀於組旒，想徂音乎珩珮。

translations.literal: Adorning the departed rites with corded tassels, recalling the departing sound in pendant ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Adorning the departed rites with corded tassels, recalling the departing sound in pendant ornaments.

sentences.zh: 悲黼筵之移御，痛翬褕之重晦。

translations.literal: Grieving that the embroidered mat seat has shifted; pained that the feathered canopy is again darkened.
translations.idiomatic: Grieving that the embroidered mat seat has shifted; pained that the feathered canopy is darkened once more.

sentences.zh: 降輿客位，撤奠殯階。

translations.literal: The carriage descends to the guest seat; the offerings are withdrawn from the bier steps.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage descends to the guest seat; the offerings are withdrawn from the bier steps.

sentences.zh: 乃命史臣，誄德述懷。

translations.literal: He then ordered the historiographer to eulogize her virtue and set forth his feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered the historiographer to eulogize her virtue and set forth his feelings.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: Its text reads:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: 倫昭儷昇，有物有憑。

translations.literal: Pattern and brightness paired in ascent — there are things, and there is what they rely upon.
translations.idiomatic: Pattern and brightness paired in ascent — there are things, and there is what they rely upon.

sentences.zh: 圓精初鑠，方祇始凝。

translations.literal: The round essence first gleams; the square earth-spirit first congeals.
translations.idiomatic: The round essence first gleams; the square earth-spirit first congeals.

sentences.zh: 昭哉世族，祥發慶膺。

translations.literal: Splendid is her clan of generations; auspicious blessing arises and felicity is received.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid is her clan of generations; auspicious blessing arises and felicity is received.

sentences.zh: 祕儀景冑，圖光玉繩。

translations.literal: Secret rites and luminous lineage; charted glory like the jade cord of stars.
translations.idiomatic: Secret rites and luminous lineage; charted glory like the jade cord of stars.

sentences.zh: 昌輝在陰，柔明將進。

translations.literal: Flourishing brilliance dwells in the yin; gentle brightness is about to advance.
translations.idiomatic: Flourishing brilliance dwells in the yin; gentle brightness is about to advance.

sentences.zh: 率禮蹈和，稱詩納順。

translations.literal: Leading ritual and treading harmony; citing poetry and receiving obedience.
translations.idiomatic: Leading ritual and treading harmony; citing poetry and receiving obedience.

sentences.zh: 爰自待年，金聲夙振。

translations.literal: From the years of waiting for marriage, her golden reputation early resounded.
translations.idiomatic: From the years of waiting for marriage, her golden reputation resounded early.

sentences.zh: 亦既有行，素章增絢。

translations.literal: Already she had conduct; plain pattern was further adorned.
translations.idiomatic: Already she had conduct; plain pattern was further adorned.

sentences.zh: 象服是加，言觀惟則。

translations.literal: Symbolic garments were added to her; her words and bearing were the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Symbolic garments were added to her; her words and bearing were the standard.

sentences.zh: 俾我王風，始基嬪德。

translations.literal: She made our royal wind begin to found consort virtue.
translations.idiomatic: She made our royal wind begin to found consort virtue.

sentences.zh: 蕙問川流，芳猷淵塞。

translations.literal: Orchid fragrance flows like a stream; fragrant plans fill the deep.
translations.idiomatic: Orchid fragrance flows like a stream; fragrant plans fill the deep.

sentences.zh: 方江泳漢，再謠南國。

translations.literal: Just as the river swims through Han, again a song for the southern realm.
translations.idiomatic: As the river flows through Han, again a song rises for the southern realm.

sentences.zh: 伊昔不造，洪化中微。

translations.literal: In those former times there was no good fortune; the great transforming influence waned at its center.
translations.idiomatic: In former times fortune failed; the great transforming influence waned at its center.

sentences.zh: 用集寶命，仰陟天機。

translations.literal: Thus gathering the precious Mandate, ascending to Heaven's design.
translations.idiomatic: Thus gathering the precious Mandate, ascending to Heaven's design.

sentences.zh: 釋位公宮，登耀紫闈。

translations.literal: Relinquishing position in the ducal palace, ascending to shine in the purple gate.
translations.idiomatic: Relinquishing position in the ducal palace, ascending to shine in the purple gate.

sentences.zh: 欽若皇姑，允迪前徽。

translations.literal: Reverently following the imperial aunt, truly continuing former excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently following the imperial aunt, truly continuing former excellence.

sentences.zh: 孝達寧親，敬行宗祀。

translations.literal: Filial piety reaching to comfort parents; respectfully performing ancestral sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Filial piety reaching to comfort parents; respectfully performing ancestral sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 進思才淑，傍綜圖史。

translations.literal: Advancing thought to talented virtue; broadly gathering charts and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing thought to talented virtue; broadly gathering charts and histories.

sentences.zh: 發音在咏，動容成紀。

translations.literal: Giving voice in song; moving countenance to form record.
translations.idiomatic: Giving voice in song; moving countenance to form record.

sentences.zh: 壼政穆宣，房樂昭理。

translations.literal: Inner governance serenely proclaimed; chamber music brightly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: Inner governance serenely proclaimed; chamber music brightly ordered.

sentences.zh: [8]坤則順成，星軒潤飾。

translations.literal: [8] The earth principle followed and completed; the star carriage moistened and adorned.
translations.idiomatic: [8] The earth principle followed and completed; the star carriage moistened and adorned.

sentences.zh: 德之所屆，惟深必測。

translations.literal: Where virtue reaches, only the deep can be fathomed.
translations.idiomatic: Where virtue reaches, only the deep can be fathomed.

sentences.zh: 下節震騰，上清朓側。

translations.literal: The lower nodes quake and rise; the upper clarity wanes on its side.
translations.idiomatic: The lower nodes quake and rise; the upper clarity wanes on its side.

sentences.zh: 有來斯雍，無思不極。

translations.literal: When they come, there is harmony; no thought fails to reach the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: When they come, there is harmony; no thought fails to reach the utmost.

sentences.zh: 謂道輔仁，司化莫晰。

translations.literal: They said the Way assists benevolence; who governs transformation is not clear.
translations.idiomatic: They said the Way assists benevolence; who governs transformation is not clear.

sentences.zh: 象物方臻，眡祲告沴。

sentences.zh: 不得如所奏。」

translations.literal: It cannot be as memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: It cannot be as memorialized."

sentences.zh: 尋崩，時年五十五。

translations.literal: Soon she died, aged fifty-five.
translations.idiomatic: Soon she died at the age of fifty-five.

sentences.zh: 遷殯東宮，門題曰崇憲宮。

translations.literal: Her coffin was moved to the Eastern Palace; the gate inscription read Chongxian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Her coffin was moved to the Eastern Palace; the gate inscription read Chongxian Palace.

sentences.zh: 上又詔曰：「朕幼集荼蓼，夙憑德訓，龕虣定業，實資仁範，恩著屯夷，有兼常慕。

translations.literal: The emperor further issued an edict: "We in youth gathered hardship, long relying on virtuous instruction; securing the fierce and settling the enterprise truly depended on benevolent model — grace marked in hardship, with doubled ordinary longing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor further issued an edict: "We in youth gathered hardship, long relying on virtuous instruction; securing the fierce and settling the enterprise truly depended on benevolent model — grace marked in hardship, with doubled ordinary longing.

sentences.zh: 夫禮沿情施，義循事立，可特齊衰三月，以申追仰之心。」

translations.literal: Since rites follow feelings in application and righteousness is established according to circumstances, we may specially wear sackcloth mourning for three months to express our heart of remembrance and reverence."
translations.idiomatic: Since rites follow feelings in application and righteousness is established according to circumstances, we may specially wear sackcloth mourning for three months to express our heart of remembrance and reverence."

sentences.zh: 諡曰昭皇太后，葬世祖陵東南，號曰脩寧陵。

translations.literal: She was posthumously styled Zhao Grand Empress Dowager, buried southeast of the Shizu Emperor's tomb, the tomb called Xiuning.
translations.idiomatic: She was posthumously styled Zhao Grand Empress Dowager, buried southeast of Emperor Shizu's tomb, the tomb called Xiuning.

sentences.zh: 先是晉安王子勛未平，巫者謂宜開昭太后陵以為厭勝。

translations.literal: Previously, before Prince Zixun of Jin'an was pacified, sorcerers said the Zhao Empress Dowager's tomb should be opened as a means of countering evil.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, before Prince Zixun of Jin'an was pacified, sorcerers said the Zhao Empress Dowager's tomb should be opened as a means of countering evil.

sentences.zh: 脩復倉卒，不得如禮。

translations.literal: The repairs were done in haste and could not follow the rites.
translations.idiomatic: The repairs were done in haste and could not follow the rites.

sentences.zh: 上性忌，慮將來致災。

translations.literal: The emperor by nature was superstitious and feared disaster would come in the future.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor by nature was superstitious and feared disaster would come in the future.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年夏，詔有司曰：「崇憲昭太后脩寧陵地，大明之世，久所考卜。

translations.literal: In summer of the fourth year of Taishi, he issued an edict the relevant offices: "The site of the Xiuning Tomb of the Chongxian Zhao Empress Dowager was long ago divined in the Daming era.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of the fourth year of Taishi, he issued an edict the relevant offices: "The site of the Xiuning Tomb of the Chongxian Zhao Empress Dowager was long ago divined in the Daming era.

sentences.zh: 前歲遭諸蕃之難，禮從權宜。

translations.literal: Last year we suffered the troubles of the various princes; the rites followed expediency.
translations.idiomatic: Last year we suffered the troubles of the various princes; the rites followed expediency.

sentences.zh: 奉營倉卒，未暇營改。

translations.literal: The construction was undertaken hastily and there was no time to build and alter.
translations.idiomatic: The construction was undertaken hastily and there was no time to rebuild and alter.

sentences.zh: 而塋隧之所，山原卑陋。

translations.literal: But the place of the tomb mound — hill and plain — was low and mean.
translations.idiomatic: But the place of the tomb mound — hill and plain — was low and mean.

sentences.zh: 頃年頹壞，日有滋甚，恒費脩整，終無永固。

translations.literal: In recent years it has crumbled, daily growing worse; constantly we spend on repairs yet never achieve lasting solidity.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years it has crumbled, daily growing worse; constantly we spend on repairs yet never achieve lasting solidity.

sentences.zh: 且詳考地形，殊乖相勢。

translations.literal: Moreover on detailed examination of the terrain, it greatly fails to match geomantic auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover on detailed examination of the terrain, it greatly fails to match geomantic auspiciousness.

sentences.zh: 朕蚤蒙慈遇，情禮兼常，思使終始之義，載彰幽顯。

translations.literal: We early received kind favor; feeling and rites both constant — we think to make the meaning of beginning to end manifest in hidden and manifest realms.
translations.idiomatic: We early received kind favor; feeling and rites both constant — we think to make the meaning of beginning to end manifest in hidden and manifest realms.

sentences.zh: 史官可就巖山左右，更宅吉地。

translations.literal: The historians may go to the left and right of Mount Yan and select a new auspicious site.
translations.idiomatic: The historians may go to the left and right of Mount Yan and select a new auspicious site.

sentences.zh: 明審龜筮，須選令辰，式遵舊典，以禮創制。

translations.literal: Clearly examine tortoise and milfoil, must choose a fine day, follow the old canon in form, and create the regulation by rites.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly examine tortoise and milfoil, must choose a fine day, follow the old canon in form, and create the regulation by rites.

sentences.zh: 今中宇雖寧，邊虜未息，營就之功，務在從簡。

translations.literal: Now though the central realm is at peace, border barbarians have not ceased; the work of completing construction should strive to be simple.
translations.idiomatic: Now though the central realm is at peace, border barbarians have not ceased; the work of completing construction should strive to be simple.

sentences.zh: 舉言尋悲，情如切割。」

translations.literal: To speak brings forth sorrow; our feelings are like cutting."
translations.idiomatic: To speak brings forth sorrow; our feelings are like cutting."

sentences.zh: 有司奏：「北疆未緝，戎役是務，禮之詳略，各沿時宜。

translations.literal: The relevant offices memorialized: "The northern frontier is not yet settled; military service is the task — whether rites are detailed or brief should each follow the time's suitability.
translations.idiomatic: The relevant offices memorialized: "The northern frontier is not yet settled; military service is the task — whether rites are detailed or brief should each follow the time's suitability.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，脩寧陵玄宮補治毀壞，權施油殿，暫出梓宮，事畢即窆，於事為允。」

translations.literal: We your ministers deliberating propose: repair damage to the Xiuning Tomb's inner chamber, provisionally erect an oiled canopy hall, temporarily remove the outer coffin, reinter as soon as the work is done — this is acceptable."
translations.idiomatic: We your ministers deliberating propose: repair damage to the Xiuning Tomb's inner chamber, provisionally erect an oiled canopy hall, temporarily remove the outer coffin, reinter as soon as the work is done — this is acceptable."

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 瓊之為衡陽內史，先后卒。

translations.literal: When Qiong was Interior Secretary of Hengyang, his first and second wives died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Qiong was Interior Secretary of Hengyang, his first and second wives died in succession.

sentences.zh: 廢帝景和中，以休之為黃門侍郎，茂之左軍將軍，並封開國縣侯，邑千戶。

translations.literal: In the Jinghe era under the deposed emperor, Xiuzhi was made Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Maozhi Left Army General; both were enfeoffed as Marquises of Kaiguo County with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jinghe era under the deposed emperor, Xiuzhi was made Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Maozhi Left Army General; both were enfeoffed as Marquises of Kaiguo County with a fief of a thousand households.

sentences.zh: 又追贈興之侍中、金紫光祿大夫，諡曰孝侯；

translations.literal: Also posthumously granted Xingzhi Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Master of the Palace with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, posthumous name Marquis Xiao;
translations.idiomatic: Also posthumously granted Xingzhi Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Master of the Palace with the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, posthumous name Marquis Xiao;

sentences.zh: 道慶散騎常侍、光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，諡曰敬侯。

translations.literal: Daoqing Regular Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness, Keeper of the Seal with the Three Excellencies' Privileges, posthumous name Marquis Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Daoqing Regular Palace Attendant, Grand Master of Brilliant Happiness, Keeper of the Seal with the Three Excellencies' Privileges, posthumous name Marquis Jing.

sentences.zh: 立道慶女為皇后，以休之為侍中，茂之黃門郎。

translations.literal: He installed Daoqing's daughter as empress, made Xiuzhi Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Maozhi Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He installed Daoqing's daughter as empress, made Xiuzhi Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Maozhi Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 太宗廢幼主，欲說太后之心，乃下令書曰：「太皇太后蚤垂愛遇，沿情即事，同於天屬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming deposed the young emperor, wishing to win the Empress Dowager's heart, he issued an order stating: "The Grand Empress Dowager early showed love and favor; following feeling and attending to matters, it is the same as kin by Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming deposed the young emperor, wishing to win the Empress Dowager's heart, he issued an order stating: "The Grand Empress Dowager early showed love and favor; following feeling and attending to matters, it is the same as kin by Heaven.

sentences.zh: 前車騎諮議參軍路休之、前丹陽丞路茂之，崇憲密戚，蚤延榮貫，並懷所勳，宜殊恒飾。

translations.literal: Former Staff Adviser to the Rapid-Cavalry General Lu Xiuzhi, former Assistant Magistrate of Danyang Lu Maozhi — close kin of Chongxian, early extended with glory and rank, both bearing meritorious service — should receive special honors beyond the ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: Former Staff Adviser to the Rapid-Cavalry General Lu Xiuzhi, former Assistant Magistrate of Danyang Lu Maozhi — close kin of Chongxian, early extended with glory and rank, both bearing meritorious service — should receive special honors beyond the ordinary.

sentences.zh: 休之可黃門侍郎，領步兵校尉；

translations.literal: Xiuzhi may be Attendant at the Yellow Gate, concurrently Colonel of Footsoldiers;
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi may be Attendant at the Yellow Gate, concurrently Colonel of Footsoldiers;

sentences.zh: 茂之可中書侍郎。」

translations.literal: Maozhi may be Attendant of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Maozhi may be Attendant of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 太宗未即位，故稱令書。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming had not yet taken the throne, hence it was called an order rather than an edict.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming had not yet taken the throne, hence it was called an order rather than an edict.

sentences.zh: 茂之又遷司徒從事中郎，休之桂陽王休範鎮北諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Maozhi was further transferred to Staff Officer of the Minister of Education; Xiuzhi became Staff Adviser to Prince Xiufan of Guiyang as Pacifying-North General.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhi was further transferred to Staff Officer of the Minister of Education; Xiuzhi became Staff Adviser to Prince Xiufan of Guiyang as Pacifying-North General.

sentences.zh: 太宗殺世祖諸子，因此陷休之等，宥其諸子。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming killed Shizu's sons and thereby framed Xiuzhi and the others, pardoning their sons.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming killed Shizu's sons and thereby framed Xiuzhi and the others, pardoning their sons.

sentences.zh: 孝武文穆王皇后諱憲嫄，琅邪臨沂人。

translations.literal: Empress of Emperor Xiaowu's Wenmu era was named Xianyuan, from Langya Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress of Emperor Xiaowu's Wenmu era was named Xianyuan, from Langya Linyi.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二十年，拜武陵王妃。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia she was invested as Princess Consort of Wuling.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Yuanjia she was invested as Princess Consort of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 生廢帝、豫章王子尚、山陰公主楚玉、臨淮康哀公主楚佩、皇女楚琇、康樂公主脩明。

translations.literal: She bore the deposed emperor, Zishang Prince of Yuzhang, the Princess of Shanyin Chuyu, the Princess Kang'ai of Linhuai Chupei, the imperial daughter Chuqiu, and the Princess of Kangle Xiuming.
translations.idiomatic: She bore the deposed emperor, Zishang Prince of Yuzhang, the Princess of Shanyin Chuyu, the Princess Kang'ai of Linhuai Chupei, the imperial daughter Chuqiu, and the Princess of Kangle Xiuming.

sentences.zh: 世祖在蕃，后甚有寵。

translations.literal: When Shizu was in his principality the empress was greatly favored.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu was in his principality the empress was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 上入伐凶逆，后留尋陽，與太后同還京都，立為皇后。

translations.literal: When the emperor entered to campaign against the wicked rebels, the empress remained at Xunyang; she returned to the capital with the empress dowager and was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor entered to campaign against the wicked rebels, the empress remained at Xunyang; she returned to the capital with the empress dowager and was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 大明四年，后率六宮躬桑于西郊，皇太后觀禮。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Daming the empress led the Six Palaces to personally mulberry-pick at the western suburb; the empress dowager observed the ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Daming the empress led the Six Palaces to personally mulberry-pick at the western suburb; the empress dowager observed the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 上下詔曰：「朕卜祥大昕，測辰拂羽，爰詔六宮，親蠶川室。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict: "We divined auspiciousness on the great propitious day, measured the time and set the plume standard, thus commanding the Six Palaces to personally tend silkworms at the river-side chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict: "We divined auspiciousness on the great propitious day, measured the time and set the plume standard, thus commanding the Six Palaces to personally tend silkworms at the river-side chamber.

sentences.zh: 皇太后降鑾從御，佇蹕觀禮。

translations.literal: The empress dowager descended her carriage to accompany, halting her train to observe the rite.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager descended her carriage to accompany, halting her train to observe the rite.

sentences.zh: 綠蘧既具，玄紞方脩，庶儀發椒，闈化動中。

translations.literal: Green cushions are ready, black sashes being prepared — various rites emanate from the inner quarters, transforming influence stirs within.
translations.idiomatic: Green cushions are ready, black sashes being prepared — various rites emanate from the inner quarters, transforming influence stirs within.

sentences.zh: 縣妃主以下，可量加班錫。」

translations.literal: County princesses, consorts and below may be granted rewards in measured degrees according to rank."
translations.idiomatic: County princesses, consorts and below may be granted rewards in measured degrees according to rank."

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，尊曰皇太后，宮曰永訓。

translations.literal: When the deposed emperor ascended the throne she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was called Yongxun.
translations.idiomatic: When the deposed emperor ascended the throne she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace was called Yongxun.

sentences.zh: 其年，崩于含章殿，時年三十八。

translations.literal: That year she died in Hanzhang Hall, aged thirty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: That year she died in Hanzhang Hall at the age of thirty-eight.

sentences.zh: 祔葬景寧陵。

translations.literal: She was buried jointly at Jingning Tomb.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried jointly at Jingning Tomb.

sentences.zh: 長子藻，位至東陽太守。

translations.literal: The eldest son Zao rose to Governor of Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest son Zao rose to Governor of Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 尚太祖第六女臨川長公主諱英媛。

translations.literal: He married Emperor Taizu's sixth daughter, the Princess Chang of Linchuan, named Yingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He married Emperor Taizu's sixth daughter, the Princess Chang of Linchuan, named Yingyuan.

sentences.zh: 公主性妒，而藻別愛左右人吳崇祖，前廢帝景和中，主讒之於廢帝，藻坐下獄死，主與王氏離婚。

translations.literal: The princess was jealous by nature; Zao separately favored his attendant Wu Chongzu. In the Jinghe era under the former deposed emperor the princess slandered him to the deposed emperor; Zao was imprisoned and died; the princess divorced the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was jealous by nature; Zao separately favored his attendant Wu Chongzu. In the Jinghe era under the former deposed emperor the princess slandered him to the deposed emperor; Zao was imprisoned and died; the princess divorced the Wang clan.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，以主適豫章太守庾沖遠，未及成禮而沖遠卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi the princess was betrothed to Governor of Yuzhang Yu Chongyuan; before the ceremony was completed Chongyuan died.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi the princess was betrothed to Governor of Yuzhang Yu Chongyuan; before the ceremony was completed Chongyuan died.

sentences.zh: 宋世諸主，莫不嚴妒，太宗每疾之。

translations.literal: All the princesses of the Song era were severely jealous without exception; Emperor Ming was always displeased by this.
translations.idiomatic: All the princesses of the Song era were severely jealous without exception; Emperor Ming was always displeased by this.

sentences.zh: 湖熟令袁慆妻以妒忌賜死，使近臣虞通之撰妒婦記。

translations.literal: The wife of Yuan Tao, Magistrate of Hushu, was sentenced to death for jealousy; he had close minister Yu Tongzhi compose a Record of Jealous Wives.
translations.idiomatic: The wife of Yuan Tao, Magistrate of Hushu, was sentenced to death for jealousy; he had close minister Yu Tongzhi compose a Record of Jealous Wives.

sentences.zh: 左光祿大夫江湛孫斅當尚世祖女，上乃使人為斅作表讓婚，曰：

translations.literal: Left Grand Master of the Palace with the Splendor of Light Jiang Zhan's grandson Jiao was to marry Shizu's daughter; the emperor had someone compose for Jiao a memorial declining the marriage, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Left Grand Master of the Palace with the Splendor of Light Jiang Zhan's grandson Jiao was to marry Shizu's daughter; the emperor had someone compose for Jiao a memorial declining the marriage, saying:

sentences.zh: 伏承詔旨，當以臨汝公主降嬪，[18]榮出望表，恩加典外。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly receives the imperial edict that the Princess of Linru will descend to become my spouse, [18] glory exceeding what was hoped, grace added beyond the ordinary canon.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant humbly receives the imperial edict that the Princess of Linru will descend to become my spouse, [18] glory exceeding what was hoped, grace added beyond the ordinary canon.

sentences.zh: 顧審輶蔽，伏用憂惶。

translations.literal: Yet considering my own obscurity and low capacity, your servant is filled with worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet considering my own obscurity and low capacity, your servant is filled with worry and fear.

sentences.zh: 臣寒門顇族，人凡質陋，閭閻有對，本隔天姻。

translations.literal: Your servant is of a cold gate and withered clan, a man of common quality and humble appearance; though our neighborhoods face each other we are originally separated by heavenly marriage ties.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant is of a cold gate and withered clan, a man of common quality and humble appearance; though our neighborhoods face each other we are originally separated by heavenly marriage ties.

sentences.zh: 如臣素流，室貧業寡，年近將冠，皆已有室，荊釵布裙，足得成禮。

translations.literal: Such as your servant's plain station: the household poor, affairs few; nearly reaching capping age, all already have spouses — thorn hairpins and cloth skirts would suffice to complete the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Such as your servant's plain station: the household poor, affairs few; nearly reaching capping age, all already have spouses — thorn hairpins and cloth skirts would suffice to complete the rites.

sentences.zh: 每不自解，無偶迄茲，媒訪莫尋，[19]素族弗問。

translations.literal: Each time I cannot understand myself — without a mate until now, matchmakers sought but not found, [19] plain clans not asked.
translations.idiomatic: Each time I cannot understand myself — without a mate until now, matchmakers sought but not found, [19] plain clans not asked.

sentences.zh: 自惟門慶，屬降公主，天恩所覃，容及醜末。

translations.literal: Reflecting on my family's honor that a princess should descend, Heaven's grace extending, indulging even an ugly last-born.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on my family's honor that a princess should descend, Heaven's grace extending, indulging even an ugly last-born.

sentences.zh: 懷憂抱惕，慮不獲免，徵命所當，果膺茲舉。

translations.literal: Bearing worry and trepidation, fearing one cannot escape; when the summons came that should be answered, truly received this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing worry and trepidation, fearing one cannot escape; when the summons came that should be answered, truly received this appointment.

sentences.zh: 雖門泰宗榮，於臣非幸，仰緣聖貸，冒陳愚實。

translations.literal: Though for the clan it is great and for the lineage glorious, for your servant it is not fortune; relying on holy indulgence, I dare state my foolish truth.
translations.idiomatic: Though for the clan it is great and for the lineage glorious, for your servant it is not fortune; relying on holy indulgence, I dare state my foolish truth.

sentences.zh: 自晉氏以來，配尚王姬者，雖累經美冑，亟有名才，至如王敦懾氣，桓溫斂威，真長佯愚以求免，子敬灸足以違詔，王偃無仲都之質，而倮露於北階，何瑀闕龍工之姿，而投軀於深井，謝莊殆自同於矇叟，[20]殷沖幾不免於強鉏。

translations.literal: Since the Jin house, those matched to imperial princesses, though repeatedly of fine lineage and often men of renown — such as Wang Dun cowed in spirit, Huan Wen reined in in awe, Zhenchang feigned stupidity to seek escape, Zijing cauterized his foot to disobey the edict, Wang Yan lacking Zhongdu's quality yet exposed naked on the north steps, He Yu lacking the dragon-craftsman's bearing yet cast his body into a deep well, Xie Zhuang nearly the same as a blind old man, [20] Yin Chong almost not escaping forced hoeing.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin house, those matched to imperial princesses, though repeatedly of fine lineage and often men of renown — such as Wang Dun cowed in spirit, Huan Wen reined in in awe, Zhenchang feigned stupidity to seek escape, Zijing cauterized his foot to disobey the edict, Wang Yan lacking Zhongdu's quality yet exposed naked on the north steps, He Yu lacking the dragon-craftsman's bearing yet cast his body into a deep well, Xie Zhuang nearly the same as a blind old man, [20] Yin Chong almost not escaping forced hoeing.

sentences.zh: 彼數人者，[21]非無才意，而勢屈於崇貴，事隔於聞覽，吞悲茹氣，無所逃訴。

translations.literal: Those several men, [21] were not without talent and intention, yet their power bent before exalted nobility, affairs blocked from imperial hearing, swallowing grief and choking on resentment with nowhere to flee or complain.
translations.idiomatic: Those several men, [21] were not without talent and intention, yet their power bent before exalted nobility, affairs blocked from imperial hearing, swallowing grief and choking on resentment with nowhere to flee or complain.

sentences.zh: 制勒甚於僕隸，防閑過於婢妾。

translations.literal: Control and restraint exceeded that over servant-boys; guard and surveillance exceeded that over maid-servants.
translations.idiomatic: Control and restraint exceeded that over servant-boys; guard and surveillance exceeded that over maid-servants.

sentences.zh: 往來出入，人理之常，當賓待客，朋從之義。

translations.literal: Coming and going in and out is the constant of human reason; receiving guests and hosting visitors is the right of companionship.
translations.idiomatic: Coming and going in and out is the constant of human reason; receiving guests and hosting visitors is the right of companionship.

sentences.zh: 而令掃轍息駕，無闚門之期；

translations.literal: Yet orders swept the ruts and halted the carriage — no date to peek at the gate;
translations.idiomatic: Yet orders swept the ruts and halted the carriage — no date to peek at the gate;

sentences.zh: 廢筵抽席，絕接對之理。

translations.literal: banquets dismantled, mats withdrawn — cutting off the principle of meeting face to face.
translations.idiomatic: banquets dismantled, mats withdrawn — cutting off the principle of meeting face to face.

sentences.zh: 非唯交友離異，乃亦兄弟疏闊。

translations.literal: Not only did friends and companions grow estranged — even brothers grew distant.
translations.idiomatic: Not only did friends and companions grow estranged — even brothers grew distant.

sentences.zh: 第令受酒肉之賜，制以動靜；

translations.literal: The house steward received gifts of wine and meat and controlled one's movements;
translations.idiomatic: The house steward received gifts of wine and meat and controlled one's movements;

sentences.zh: 監子荷錢帛之私，節其言笑。

translations.literal: the chief attendant carried private money and silk and regulated one's speech and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: the chief attendant carried private money and silk and regulated one's speech and laughter.

sentences.zh: 姆嬭爭媚，相勸以嚴；

translations.literal: Nurses and wet-nurses competed in flattery, urging each other to severity;
translations.idiomatic: Nurses and wet-nurses vied in flattery, each urging the other to be severe;

sentences.zh: 妮媼競前，相諂以急。

translations.literal: old matrons vied to advance, flattering each other with haste.
translations.idiomatic: old matrons vied to advance, flattering each other with haste.

sentences.zh: 第令必凡庸下才，監子皆葭萌愚豎，議舉止則未閑是非，聽言語則謬於虛實。

translations.literal: House stewards are invariably mediocre inferior talents; chief attendants are all budding fools — judging conduct they do not understand right from wrong, hearing speech they err on truth and falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: House stewards are invariably mediocre inferior talents; chief attendants are all budding fools — judging conduct they do not understand right from wrong, hearing speech they err on truth and falsehood.

sentences.zh: 姆嬭敢恃耆舊，唯贊妒忌，尼媼自倡多知，務檢口舌。

translations.literal: Nurses dare rely on senior standing only to praise jealousy; nuns pose as knowing much, bent on policing the tongue.
translations.idiomatic: Nurses dare rely on senior standing only to praise jealousy; nuns pose as knowing much, bent on policing the tongue.

sentences.zh: 其間又有應答問訊，卜筮師母，乃至殘餘飲食，詰辯與誰，衣被故敝，必責頭領。

translations.literal: Among them are also answering inquiries, diviners and midwives, even leftover food and drink — interrogated as to who shared them; old worn clothing — the steward is always blamed.
translations.idiomatic: Among them are also answering inquiries, diviners and midwives, even leftover food and drink — interrogated as to who shared them; old worn clothing — the steward is always blamed.

sentences.zh: 又出入之宜，繁省難衷，或進不獲前，或入不聽出。

translations.literal: Also the propriety of going in and out — whether elaborate or simple is hard to reconcile; sometimes one could not advance, sometimes one entered but was not allowed to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Also the propriety of going in and out — whether elaborate or simple is hard to reconcile; sometimes one could not advance, sometimes one entered but was not allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 不入則嫌於欲疏，求出則疑有別意，召必以三晡為期，遣必以日出為限，夕不見晚魄，朝不識曙星。

translations.literal: Not entering then suspected of wishing estrangement; seeking to leave then suspected of other intent — summons must be by the third watch before dusk, dismissal must be by sunrise; evenings without seeing the late moon, mornings without recognizing the dawn stars.
translations.idiomatic: Not entering then suspected of wishing estrangement; seeking to leave then suspected of other intent — summons must be by the third watch before dusk, dismissal must be by sunrise; evenings without seeing the late moon, mornings without recognizing the dawn stars.

sentences.zh: 至於夜步月而弄琴，晝拱袂而披卷，一生之內，與此長乖。

translations.literal: As for strolling by moonlight at night playing the zither, by day holding sleeves reading scrolls — within one lifetime, long estranged from these.
translations.idiomatic: As for strolling by moonlight at night playing the zither, by day holding sleeves reading scrolls — within one lifetime, long estranged from these.

sentences.zh: 又聲影裁聞，則少婢奔迸；

translations.literal: Also at the slightest sound or shadow young maidservants would rush about;
translations.idiomatic: Also at the slightest sound or shadow young maidservants would rush about;

sentences.zh: 裾袂向席，則老醜叢來。

translations.literal: when a hem or sleeve turned toward the mat old ugly women would crowd in.
translations.idiomatic: when a hem or sleeve turned toward the mat old ugly women would crowd in.

sentences.zh: 左右整刷，以疑寵見嫌；

translations.literal: Attendants grooming and combing — suspected of favored love and seen with jealousy;
translations.idiomatic: Attendants grooming and combing — suspected of favored love and seen with jealousy;

sentences.zh: 賓客未冠，以少容致斥。

translations.literal: guests not yet capped — rejected on account of youthful appearance.
translations.idiomatic: guests not yet capped — rejected on account of youthful appearance.

sentences.zh: 禮則有列媵，象則有貫魚，本無嫚嫡之嫌，豈有輕婦之誚。

translations.literal: In rites there are ranked secondary consorts; in symbolism there are strung fish — originally no suspicion of slighting the principal wife, how could there be rebuke for favoring a lesser wife?
translations.idiomatic: In rites there are ranked secondary consorts; in symbolism there are strung fish — originally no suspicion of slighting the principal wife, how could there be rebuke for favoring a lesser wife?

sentences.zh: 況今義絕傍私，虔恭正匹，而每事必言無儀適，設辭輒言輕易我。

translations.literal: Moreover now the rite forbids side attachments — reverently honoring the proper spouse — yet on every matter must speak of improper conduct, and every argument says I am treated lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover now the rite forbids side attachments — reverently honoring the proper spouse — yet on every matter must speak of improper conduct, and every argument says I am treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 又竊聞諸主集聚，唯論夫族。

translations.literal: Also your servant has secretly heard that when princesses gather they speak only of their husbands' families.
translations.idiomatic: Also your servant has secretly heard that when princesses gather they speak only of their husbands' families.

sentences.zh: 緩不足為急者法，急則可為緩者師，更相扇誘，本其恒意，不可貸借，固實常辭。

translations.literal: The lenient not adequate as models for the strict — the strict may serve as teachers for the lenient; egging each other on, each stating her usual view that no grace may be extended — this is indeed their constant phrase.
translations.idiomatic: The lenient not adequate as models for the strict — the strict may serve as teachers for the lenient; egging each other on, each stating her usual view that no grace may be extended — this is indeed their constant phrase.

sentences.zh: 或言野敗去，或言人笑我，雖家曰私理，有甚王憲，發口所言，恒同科律。

translations.literal: Some say the husband was defeated and driven off, some say people laugh at me — though the household calls it a private matter, it exceeds royal statutes; words spoken are always on the same level as penal law.
translations.idiomatic: Some say the husband was defeated and driven off, some say people laugh at me — though the household calls it a private matter, it exceeds royal statutes; words spoken are always on the same level as penal law.

sentences.zh: 王藻雖復強佷，頗經學涉，戲笑之事，遂為寃魂。

translations.literal: Though Wang Zao was again stubborn and harsh, he had considerable learning — a matter of jest became a wronged spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wang Zao was again stubborn and harsh, he had considerable learning — a matter of jest became a wronged spirit.

sentences.zh: 褚曖憂憤，用致夭絕。

translations.literal: Chu Ai, through worry and anger, came to early death.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Ai, through worry and anger, came to early death.

sentences.zh: 傷理害義，難以具聞。

translations.literal: Injuring reason and harming righteousness — too much to recite fully.
translations.idiomatic: Injuring reason and harming righteousness — too much to recite fully.

sentences.zh: 夫螽斯之德，實致克昌；

translations.literal: The virtue of the locust hives truly brings flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of the locust hives truly brings flourishing;

sentences.zh: 專妒之行，有妨繁衍。

translations.literal: Exclusive jealousy has impeded propagation.
translations.idiomatic: Exclusive jealousy has impeded propagation.

sentences.zh: 是以尚主之門，往往絕嗣；

translations.literal: Thus the gates of those who marry princesses often end up without heirs;
translations.idiomatic: Thus the gates of those who marry princesses often end up without heirs;

sentences.zh: 駙馬之身，通離釁咎。

translations.literal: the bodies of imperial sons-in-law constantly suffer separation and blame.
translations.idiomatic: the bodies of imperial sons-in-law constantly suffer separation and blame.

sentences.zh: 以臣凡弱，何以克堪。

translations.literal: Your servant being common and weak — how could he bear it?
translations.idiomatic: Your servant being common and weak — how could he bear it?

sentences.zh: 必將毀族淪門，豈伊身眚。

translations.literal: It will surely ruin the clan and overthrow the gate — not merely his body's misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: It will surely ruin the clan and overthrow the gate — not merely his body's misfortune.

sentences.zh: 前後嬰此，其人雖眾，然皆患彰遐邇，事隔天朝，故吞言咽理，無敢論訴。

translations.literal: Before and after afflicted by this — though many the men — yet all sufferings were manifest far and near, affairs blocked by the heavenly court; hence they swallowed words and choked on reason, none daring to petition and complain.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after afflicted by this — though many the men — yet all sufferings were manifest far and near, affairs blocked by the heavenly court; hence they swallowed words and choked on reason, none daring to petition and complain.

sentences.zh: 臣幸屬聖明，矜照由道，弘物以典，處親以公，臣之鄙懷，可得自盡。

translations.literal: Your servant fortunately belongs to a sage and bright reign that pities and illuminates according to the Way, enlarges things by canon, treats kin with fairness — my humble sentiments may be fully expressed.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant fortunately belongs to a sage and bright reign that pities and illuminates according to the Way, enlarges things by canon, treats kin with fairness — my humble sentiments may be fully expressed.

sentences.zh: 如臣門分，世荷殊榮，足守前基，便預提拂，清官顯宦，或由才升，一叨婚戚，咸成恩假。

translations.literal: As for your servant's clan station — generations bearing special glory, sufficient to guard the former foundation, then prematurely lifted and groomed — clear offices and prominent posts might sometimes rise by talent; once tainted with marriage kinship, all become favors granted.
translations.idiomatic: As for your servant's clan station — generations bearing special glory, sufficient to guard the former foundation, then prematurely lifted and groomed — clear offices and prominent posts might sometimes rise by talent; once tainted with marriage kinship, all become favors granted.

sentences.zh: [22]是以仰冒非宜，披露丹實。

translations.literal: [22] Therefore I impertinently presume the unsuitable and disclose my sincere truth.
translations.idiomatic: [22] Therefore I impertinently presume the unsuitable and disclose my sincere truth.

sentences.zh: 非唯止陳一己，規全身願；

translations.literal: Not only to state my own case and scheme for self-preservation;
translations.idiomatic: Not only to state my own case and scheme for self-preservation;

sentences.zh: 實乃廣申諸門憂患之切。

translations.literal: truly to broadly declare the acute grief of all such households.
translations.idiomatic: truly to broadly declare the acute grief of all such households.

sentences.zh: 伏願天慈照察，特賜蠲停，使燕雀微羣，得保叢蔚，蠢物含生，自己彌篤。

translations.literal: I prostrate myself and hope Heaven's compassion will examine and see, specially grant exemption and cessation, so that swallow-and-sparrow petty groups may preserve thickets and shade, stupid creatures bearing life may themselves be ever more devoted.
translations.idiomatic: I prostrate myself and hope Your Heaven-sent compassion will examine the matter and specially grant exemption, so that humble folk like swallows and sparrows may keep their thickets and shade, and witless creatures bearing life may thereby grow ever more devoted.

sentences.zh: 若恩詔難降，披請不申，便當刊膚剪髮，投山竄海。

translations.literal: If gracious edicts are hard to descend and petitions laid bare are not granted, then one should shave flesh and cut hair, throw oneself into mountains and burrow into the sea.
translations.idiomatic: If gracious edicts cannot be issued and our open plea goes unheeded, we shall shave our flesh and cut our hair and flee to the mountains or burrow into the sea.

sentences.zh: 太宗以此表徧示諸主。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong took this memorial and broadly showed it to all the princesses.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming circulated this memorial among all the princesses for them to see.

sentences.zh: 於是臨川長公主上表曰：「妾遭隨奇薄，絕於王氏，私庭囂戾，致此分異。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Princess of Linchuan memorialized: "Your handmaiden encountered cruelly meager fortune, was cut off from the Wang clan; the private household was clamorous and perverse, causing this separation.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Princess of Linchuan submitted a memorial: "Your handmaiden met with cruelly meager fortune and was severed from the Wang clan; the private household grew clamorous and abusive, which brought about this rupture.

sentences.zh: 今孤疾煢然，假息朝夕，情寄所鍾，唯在一子。

translations.literal: Now alone, ill, and desolate, borrowing breath morning and evening, where feeling lodges and is treasured — only in one son.
translations.idiomatic: Now I am alone, ill, and desolate, living on borrowed breath from day to day; the one to whom my heart is devoted is my single son.

sentences.zh: 契闊荼炭，持兼憐愍，否泰枯榮，繫以為命。

translations.literal: Parting and reunion, thorn and fire — holding them together with pity; adversity and ease, withering and flourishing — bound as my life.
translations.idiomatic: Parting and reunion, hardship and suffering — I hold them together with pity; whether in adversity or ease, withering or flourishing, my life hangs upon him.

sentences.zh: 實願申其門釁，還為母子。

translations.literal: Truly I wish to declare the clan's stigma and return to being mother and son.
translations.idiomatic: I earnestly wish to clear the stain upon our clan's name and be restored as mother and son.

sentences.zh: 推遷僶俛，未及自聞。

translations.literal: Delayed in time, bowing deferentially — not yet able to report on my own.
translations.idiomatic: Time has passed while I bowed in deferential silence, unable until now to speak for myself.

sentences.zh: 先朝慈愛，鑑妾丹衷。

translations.literal: The former emperor's loving kindness discerned your handmaiden's sincere heart.
translations.idiomatic: The former emperor in his loving kindness saw into your handmaiden's sincere heart.

sentences.zh: 若賜使息徹歸第定省，仰揆天旨，或有可尋。

translations.literal: If granted to send my son Che home to his residence for attendance and visits, looking up to measure Heaven's intent, there may be something to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: If you would permit my son Che to return home for regular visits, and I look up to discern Heaven's intent, there may yet be grounds for reconciliation.

sentences.zh: 今事迫誠切，不顧典憲，敢緣恩燾，觸冒披聞。

translations.literal: Now the matter presses with sincere urgency; disregarding statutes and regulations, I dare rely on enveloping grace and touch offense by laying bare my plea.
translations.idiomatic: The matter now presses upon me with urgent sincerity; disregarding law and regulation, I dare rely on your enveloping grace and impertinently lay my plea before you.

sentences.zh: 特乞還身王族，守養弱嗣。

translations.literal: Specially I beg to return my person to the Wang clan and guard and nurture the weak heir.
translations.idiomatic: I specially beg to be received back into the Wang clan and to guard and nurture my young heir.

sentences.zh: 雖死之日，實甘於生。」

translations.literal: Though the day of death — truly sweeter than life."
translations.idiomatic: Even the day of my death would be sweeter than life itself."

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: Permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Her request was granted.

sentences.zh: 藻弟懋，昇明末貴達。

translations.literal: Zao's younger brother Mao, at the end of the Shengming era attained noble eminence.
translations.idiomatic: Zao's younger brother Mao rose to high rank and eminence at the end of the Shengming era.

sentences.zh: 懋弟攸，太宰從事中郎。

translations.literal: Mao's younger brother You, Attendant Gentleman in the Grand Tutor's suite.
translations.idiomatic: Mao's younger brother You served as Attendant Gentleman in the Grand Tutor's office.

sentences.zh: 蚤卒，追贈黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He died young; posthumously enfeoffed as Yellow Gate Attendant.
