translations.idiomatic: He died young and was posthumously granted the title Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 弟臻，昇明末顯宦。

translations.literal: Younger brother Zhen, at the end of the Shengming era held prominent office.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Zhen held high office at the end of the Shengming era.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝何皇后諱令婉，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: The Deposed Former Emperor He's Empress, tabooed name Lingwan, was a native of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress He of the Former Deposed Emperor, whose personal name was Lingwan, came from Qian in Lujiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年，納為皇太子妃，大明五年，薨于東宮徽光殿，時年十七。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian she was taken in as Crown Princess; in the fifth year of Daming she died in the Eastern Palace's Huiguang Hall, aged seventeen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xiaojian she was installed as crown princess; in the fifth year of Daming she died in Huiguang Hall of the Eastern Palace, at the age of seventeen.

sentences.zh: 葬□□，諡曰獻妃。

translations.literal: Buried at □□, posthumous title Xian Consort.
translations.idiomatic: She was buried at □□ [text lost] and given the posthumous title Consort Xian.

sentences.zh: 上更為太子置內職二等，曰保林，曰良娣。

translations.literal: The emperor again for the crown prince established two ranks of inner offices, called Baolin and Liangdi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then established two ranks of inner palace posts for the crown prince, Baolin and Liangdi.

sentences.zh: 納南中郎長史太山羊瞻女為良娣，宜都太守袁僧惠女為保林。

translations.literal: He took in the daughter of Yang Zhan of Taishan, Senior Clerk of the Southern Palace Gentleman, as Liangdi; the daughter of Yuan Senghui, Administrator of Yidu, as Baolin.
translations.idiomatic: He took Yang Zhan of Taishan's daughter — Senior Clerk of the Southern Palace Attendant — as Liangdi, and Yuan Senghui of Yidu commandery's daughter as Baolin.

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，追崇獻妃曰獻皇后。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor acceded, he elevated in pursuit Xian Consort to Xian Empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he posthumously elevated Consort Xian to Empress Xian.

sentences.zh: 太宗踐阼，遷后與廢帝合葬龍山北。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended, he moved the empress to be jointly buried with the Deposed Emperor north of Long Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming took the throne, he reinterred the empress to be buried jointly with the Deposed Emperor north of Long Mountain.

sentences.zh: 瑀兄子亮，孝建初，為桂陽太守。

translations.literal: Yu's elder brother's son Liang, at the beginning of Xiaojian, was Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's nephew Liang served as Administrator of Guiyang at the beginning of the Xiaojian era.

sentences.zh: 丞相南郡王義宣為逆，遣參軍王師壽斷桂陽道，以防廣州刺史宗慤，亮收斬之。

translations.literal: The Chancellor, Prince of Nanjun Yixuan, rebelled; he sent Staff Officer Wang Shishou to cut the Guiyang road to block Guangzhou Inspector Zong Que; Liang captured and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chancellor, Prince of Nanjun Yixuan, rebelled, he dispatched Staff Officer Wang Shishou to cut the Guiyang route so as to block Guangzhou Inspector Zong Que; Liang captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: [24]官至新安內史。

translations.literal: [24] His office reached Inner Administrator of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: [24] He rose to the post of Inner Administrator of Xin'an.

sentences.zh: 亮弟恢，廢帝元徽初，為廣州剌史，未之鎮，坐國哀朞晦不到，免官。

translations.literal: Liang's younger brother Hui, at the beginning of Yuanhui of the Deposed Emperor, was Inspector of Guangzhou; before reaching his post, he was charged with failing to arrive on the dark day of national mourning at term's end — dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's younger brother Hui, at the start of the Yuanhui era under the Deposed Emperor, was appointed Inspector of Guangzhou; before he took up the post he was dismissed for failing to appear on the dark day marking the end of the period of national mourning.

sentences.zh: 復起為都官尚書，未拜，卒。

translations.literal: Again raised as Minister of Justice; before accepting appointment, died.
translations.idiomatic: He was reappointed Minister of Justice but died before he could accept the commission.

sentences.zh: 恢弟誕，司徒右長史。

translations.literal: Hui's younger brother Yan, Senior Clerk on the right of the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's younger brother Yan served as Senior Clerk on the right in the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 誕弟衍，最知名。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Yan — most renowned in name.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Yan was the best known of the family.

sentences.zh: 性躁動。

translations.literal: By nature restless and agitated.
translations.idiomatic: He was restless and impulsive by nature.

sentences.zh: 太宗初，為建安王休仁司徒從事中郎，仍除黃門郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taizong's reign, he was Attendant Gentleman in the Ministry of Works of Prince Jian'an Xiuren; then appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Ming's reign he served as Attendant Gentleman in the Ministry of Works under Prince Jian'an Xiuren, and was then appointed Yellow Gate Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 未拜竟，求轉司徒司馬。

translations.literal: Before the appointment was fully concluded, he requested transfer to Marshal of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had even formally assumed the Yellow Gate post, he asked to be transferred to Marshal of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 得司馬，復求太子右率。

translations.literal: Obtaining Marshal, again requested Right Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had the marshal's post, he asked again for Right Leader of the Crown Prince's Guard.

sentences.zh: 拜右率一二日，復求侍中。

translations.literal: Appointed Right Leader for a day or two, again requested Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: After only a day or two as Right Leader, he asked again to be made Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 旬日之間，求進無已。

translations.literal: Within ten days' span, seeking advancement without end.
translations.idiomatic: Within a fortnight his demands for promotion knew no end.

sentences.zh: 不得侍中，以怨詈賜死。

translations.literal: Not obtaining Attendant-in-Ordinary — because of resentful cursing, granted death.
translations.idiomatic: When he failed to obtain the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary, he was executed by imperial order for cursing in resentment.

sentences.zh: 以太后弟道慶為給事中。

translations.literal: He made the Empress Dowager's younger brother Daoqing a Supplicant Within the Gates.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed the Empress Dowager's younger brother Daoqing Supplicant Within the Gates.

sentences.zh: 泰始三年卒，追贈通直散騎常侍，賜爵縣侯。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi he died; posthumously granted Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry and enfeoffed as District Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Taishi and was posthumously made Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and Cavalry and enfeoffed as District Marquis.

sentences.zh: 又追贈太后父散騎常侍，母王氏成樂鄉君。

translations.literal: Again posthumously granted the Empress Dowager's father Regular Attendant of Cavalry, her mother Lady Wang as Lady of Chengle Township.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager's father was also posthumously made Regular Attendant of Cavalry, and her mother, Lady Wang, was made Lady of Chengle Township.

sentences.zh: 上嘗宮內大集，而臝婦人觀之，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: The emperor once held a great gathering within the palace, and naked women watched it for mirth and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once held a great gathering inside the palace at which naked women were made to watch as a source of amusement.

sentences.zh: 后以扇障面，獨無所言。

translations.literal: The empress used a fan to screen her face, alone saying nothing.
translations.idiomatic: The empress screened her face with a fan and alone said nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝怒曰：「外舍家寒乞，今共為笑樂，何獨不視？」

translations.literal: The emperor angrily said: "Outsider's household — cold and beggarly — now we share in laughter and joy; why alone do you not look?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said angrily: "You come from an outsider's cold and beggarly household — now we are all sharing this mirth; why will you alone not look?"

sentences.zh: 后曰：「為樂之事，其方自多。

translations.literal: The empress said: "For matters of pleasure, the methods naturally are many.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said: "There are many proper ways to take pleasure.

sentences.zh: 豈有姑姊妹集聚，而臝婦人形體。

translations.literal: How could there be a gathering of sisters-in-law and sisters, yet naked women's bodies?
translations.idiomatic: How can one gather with sisters-in-law and female kin and expose the naked bodies of women?

sentences.zh: 以此為樂，外舍之為歡適，實與此不同。」

translations.literal: Taking this as pleasure — what outsiders take for joyful ease is truly not the same as this."
translations.idiomatic: To take this as pleasure — what we outsiders call true enjoyment is altogether different."

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，遣后令起。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and sent the empress away, ordering her to rise and leave.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and had the empress dismissed.

sentences.zh: 后兄揚州刺史景文以此事語從舅陳郡謝緯曰：「后在家為儜弱婦人，不知今段遂能剛正如此。」

translations.literal: The empress's elder brother Yangzhou Inspector Jingwen on this matter spoke to maternal uncle Xie Wei of Chen commandery, saying: "The empress at home was a weak and timid woman — I did not know that in this matter she could be so upright and firm."
translations.idiomatic: The empress's elder brother, Yangzhou Inspector Jingwen, told their maternal uncle Xie Wei of Chen commandery about the affair: "At home the empress was a weak and timid woman — I never imagined she could be so upright and firm as this."

sentences.zh: 廢帝即位，尊為皇太后，宮曰弘訓。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor acceded, she was honored as Empress Dowager; her palace named Hongxun.
translations.idiomatic: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager, with her residence named Hongxun.

sentences.zh: 廢帝失德，太后每加勗譬，始者猶見順從，後狂慝轉甚，漸不悅。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor lost virtue; the Empress Dowager each time added exhortation and admonition — at first he still appeared compliant, afterward wicked madness turned ever worse, and gradually she was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: As the Deposed Emperor's conduct deteriorated, the Empress Dowager repeatedly exhorted and admonished him; at first he still seemed compliant, but as his wild depravity worsened she grew increasingly displeased.

sentences.zh: 元徽五年五月五日，太后賜帝玉柄毛扇，帝嫌其毛柄不華，因此欲加酖害，已令太醫煑藥，左右人止之曰：「若行此事，官便應作孝子，豈復得出入狡獪。」

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Yuanhui, the Empress Dowager gifted the emperor a feather fan with jade handle; the emperor disliked that the feather handle was not ornate, and because of this wished to add poison-harm; he had already ordered the Imperial Physician to boil medicine; attendants left and right stopped him, saying: "If this matter is carried out, Your Majesty would have to act the filial son — how could you again go in and out with roguish sport?"
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month in the fifth year of Yuanhui, the Empress Dowager gave the emperor a feather fan with a jade handle; the emperor disliked the plain feather handle and therefore plotted to poison her; he had already ordered the imperial physician to brew the drug, but attendants stopped him, saying: "If you do this, Your Majesty will have to play the filial son — how then could you roam about in roguish freedom?"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「汝語大有理。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Your words have great reason."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "You speak with great sense."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: Thereupon he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: And so he desisted.

sentences.zh: 明帝陳貴妃諱妙登，丹陽建康人，屠家女也。

translations.literal: Ming Emperor's Honored Consort Chen, tabooed name Miaodeng, was a native of Jiankang in Danyang — a butcher's family's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Honored Consort Chen of Emperor Ming, whose personal name was Miaodeng, came from Jiankang in Danyang commandery; she was the daughter of a butcher's family.

sentences.zh: 世祖常使尉司採訪民間子女有姿色者。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizu constantly had guard offices search out among the people daughters of good appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu regularly sent guard officers to seek out among the common people young women of fine appearance.

sentences.zh: 太妃家在建康縣界，家貧，有草屋兩三間。

translations.literal: The Grand Consort's family was within Jiankang county bounds; the family was poor, with two or three grass-thatched huts.
translations.idiomatic: Her family lived within Jiankang county; they were poor and had only two or three thatched huts.

sentences.zh: 上出行，問尉曰：「御道邊那得此草屋，當由家貧。」

translations.literal: The emperor went out on a journey and asked the guard officer: "How does this grass hut come beside the imperial road? It must be because the family is poor."
translations.idiomatic: On an outing the emperor asked the guard officer: "How does a grass hut come to be beside the imperial road? The family must be poor."

sentences.zh: 賜錢三萬，令起瓦屋。

translations.literal: He granted thirty thousand cash and ordered them to raise a tile-roofed house.
translations.idiomatic: He granted thirty thousand cash and ordered a tiled house built for them.

sentences.zh: 尉自送錢與之，家人並不在，唯太妃在家，時年十二三。

translations.literal: The guard officer himself delivered the money to them; all family members were away — only the Grand Consort was at home, then twelve or thirteen years of age.
translations.idiomatic: The guard officer delivered the money himself; none of her family were home — only she was there, twelve or thirteen years old at the time.

sentences.zh: 尉見其容質甚美，即以白世祖，於是迎入宮。

translations.literal: The guard officer saw her countenance and quality were very beautiful and immediately reported to Emperor Shizu; thereupon she was welcomed into the palace.
translations.idiomatic: The guard officer saw how beautiful she was and reported it at once to Emperor Xiaowu, and she was brought into the palace.

sentences.zh: 在路太后房內，經二三年，再呼，不見幸。

translations.literal: She was in the Empress Dowager's chambers — through two or three years, twice summoned, never favored.
translations.idiomatic: She remained in the Empress Dowager's chambers for two or three years; though summoned twice, she never received the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 太后因言於上，以賜太宗。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager thereupon spoke to the emperor and had her granted to Emperor Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager spoke to the emperor and had her given to Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 始有寵，一年許衰歇，以乞李道兒。

translations.literal: At first she had favor; after about a year favor waned, and she was given to Li Dao'er.
translations.idiomatic: At first she won his favor, but after about a year it faded, and he gave her away to Li Dao'er.

sentences.zh: 尋又迎還，生廢帝，故民中皆呼廢帝為李氏子。

translations.literal: Soon again welcomed back; bore the Deposed Emperor — hence among the people all called the Deposed Emperor Li's son.
translations.idiomatic: Before long she was brought back; she bore the Deposed Emperor, and so among the people he was widely called Li's son.

sentences.zh: 廢帝後每自稱李將軍，或自謂李統。

translations.literal: The Deposed Emperor afterward often styled himself General Li, or called himself Li Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Deposed Emperor often styled himself General Li, or called himself Commander Li.

sentences.zh: 伯父照宗，中書通事舍人。

translations.literal: Paternal uncle Zhao Zong, General Purpose Attendant of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Her paternal uncle Zhao Zong served as General Attendant of Affairs at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 叔佛念，步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Paternal uncle Fonian, Colonel of Footsoldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Her uncle Fonian served as Colonel of the Footsoldiers.

sentences.zh: 兄敬元，通直郎，南魯郡太守。

translations.literal: Elder brother Jingyuan, Attendant of Direct Communication, Administrator of Nanlu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Her elder brother Jingyuan served as Attendant of Direct Communication and Administrator of Nanlu commandery.

sentences.zh: 佛念大通貨賄，侵亂朝政。

translations.literal: Fonian greatly trafficked in goods and bribes, encroaching upon and disturbing court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Fonian engaged heavily in bribery and corrupt trade, disrupting court governance.

sentences.zh: 昇明初，賜死。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shengming, granted death.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Shengming era he was executed by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝江皇后諱簡珪，濟陽考城人，北中郎長史智淵孫女。

translations.literal: Later Deposed Emperor Jiang Empress, tabooed name Jiangui, native of Kaocheng in Jiyang — granddaughter of Senior Clerk of the Northern Palace Gentleman Zhiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jiang of the Later Deposed Emperor, whose personal name was Jiangui, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery; she was the granddaughter of Senior Clerk Zhiyuan of the Northern Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 泰始五年，太宗訪求太子妃，而雅信小數，名家女多不合。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi, Emperor Taizong sought a crown princess; he greatly trusted minor arts of calculation — noble-house daughters mostly did not match.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Taishi, Emperor Ming sought a crown princess; as he greatly trusted divination, daughters of eminent families mostly failed to match the auguries.

sentences.zh: 后弱小，門無強廕，以卜筮最吉，故為太子納之。

translations.literal: The empress was young and small; her gate had no powerful shelter — because divination and milfoil were most auspicious, therefore for the crown prince she was taken in.
translations.idiomatic: The future empress was young and slight, and her family lacked powerful patronage; because divination proved most auspicious, the crown prince took her in marriage.

sentences.zh: 諷朝士州郡令獻物，多者將直百金。

translations.literal: He hinted to court gentlemen and prefectures and commanderies to present gifts — those with much approached a value of a hundred gold.
translations.idiomatic: He strongly hinted that court officials and local magistrates should present gifts — the most lavish were worth nearly a hundred gold pieces.

sentences.zh: 始興太守孫奉伯止獻琴書，其外無餘物。

translations.literal: Shixing Administrator Sun Fengbo only presented zither and books — beyond that no surplus goods.
translations.idiomatic: Shixing Administrator Sun Fengbo presented only a zither and books — nothing else besides.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，封藥賜死，既而原之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered, sealed medicine and granted death — afterward pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor flew into a rage and sent sealed poison with orders for his execution, but then pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 太子即帝位，立為皇后。

translations.literal: The crown prince immediately took the imperial position; established her as empress.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince ascended the throne, she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 帝既廢，降為蒼梧王妃。

translations.literal: Once the emperor was deposed, demoted to Lady of the Prince of Cangwu.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor was deposed, she was demoted to Princess Consort of Cangwu.

sentences.zh: 智淵自有傳。

translations.literal: Zhiyuan has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyuan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 順帝謝皇后諱梵境，陳郡陽夏人，右光祿大夫莊孫女也。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun's Empress Xie, tabooed name Fanjing, native of Yangxia in Chen commandery — granddaughter of Right Grand Master of Splendor Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xie of Emperor Shun, whose personal name was Fanjing, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery; she was the granddaughter of Right Grand Master of Splendor Xie Zhuang.

sentences.zh: 昇明二年，立為皇后。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shengming, established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Shengming she was made empress.

sentences.zh: 順帝禪位，降為汝陰王妃。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shun abdicated the throne, demoted to Lady of the Prince of Runan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shun abdicated, she was reduced to Princess Consort of Runan.

sentences.zh: 莊自有傳。

translations.literal: Zhuang has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：飲食男女，人之大欲存焉。

translations.literal: The historian says: Food, drink, male and female — in these man's great desires reside.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Food, drink, and sexual desire — in these lie humanity's greatest appetites.

sentences.zh: [28]故聖人順民情而為之度，王宮六列，士室二等，皆司事設防，典文曲立。

translations.literal: [28] Therefore the sage men followed the people's feelings and set bounds for them; the royal palace's six ranks, the scholar's chamber's two grades — all assigned duties and set barriers, canonical texts intricately established.
translations.idiomatic: [28] Therefore the sages followed the people's inclinations and set bounds accordingly: the six ranks of the royal harem and the two grades permitted to gentlemen were all offices with defined duties and safeguards, established in canonical law.

sentences.zh: 若夫義篤閫闈，化形邦國，古先哲王有以之致治者矣。

translations.literal: As for righteousness deep within the inner gate, transforming form in the state — ancient sage kings have by this achieved good governance.
translations.idiomatic: When righteousness is cultivated within the inner quarters and its influence shapes the state, ancient sage-kings have indeed achieved good governance thereby.

sentences.zh: 夫后妃專夕，配以德升；

translations.literal: Empresses and consorts monopolize the night, matched and raised by virtue;
translations.idiomatic: Empresses and consorts were to monopolize the royal bedchamber, elevated by virtue rather than beauty;

sentences.zh: 姬嬙並御，進非色幸。

translations.literal: Jis and Qiangs jointly attended, advancement not by color-favor.
translations.idiomatic: secondary consorts shared attendance, advancement not granted through physical favor alone.

sentences.zh: 欲使情有覃被，愛罔偏流，專貞內表，妖蠱外息。

translations.literal: Wishing to make feeling have spreading cover, love without partial flow, exclusive fidelity shown within, demonic sorcery extinguished without.
translations.idiomatic: The aim was that affection be broadly shared, love not narrowly channeled — exclusive fidelity within, and seductive intrigue stilled without.

sentences.zh: 至於娉納有章，俔天作儷，必四岳之後。

translations.literal: As for betrothal and reception having pattern, matching Heaven to make pairs — must be from the Four Peaks' descendants.
translations.idiomatic: As for marriage and reception, rites were fixed: to match Heaven in taking a consort required a daughter of the Four Peaks.

sentences.zh: 雖正位天閨，禮亢尊極，而衰厭易兆，恩宴難留，一謝屬車之塵，永隔青蒲之地。

translations.literal: Although occupying correct position in Heaven's inner gate, rites exalted to utmost honor — yet decline and satiety easily foretoken, gracious feasts hard to retain; once departed the dust of the attending carriage, forever separated from the green rush mat ground.
translations.idiomatic: Though one might hold the highest place in the inner palace and receive the most exalted rites, weariness comes easily and royal favor is hard to hold; once one falls behind the imperial procession's dust, one is forever cut off from the green rush mats of the inner court.

sentences.zh: 是故元后慎終，良有以也。

translations.literal: Therefore the primary consort is careful to the end — truly there is reason for it.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the chief consort must be careful to the end — and with good reason.

sentences.zh: 自元嘉以降，內職稍繁，椒庭綺觀，千門萬戶，而淫粧怪飾，變炫無窮。

translations.literal: From Yuankai onward, inner offices gradually multiplied; pepper-courtyard brocade halls, a thousand gates and ten thousand doorways — yet licentious adornment and strange ornament changed and dazzled without end.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yuankai era onward, inner-palace offices gradually multiplied; brocade halls opened in the inner quarters with a thousand gates and ten thousand doorways, and wanton dress and bizarre ornament shifted and dazzled without end.

sentences.zh: 自漢氏昭陽之輪奐，魏室九華之照曜，曾不能概其萬一。

translations.literal: Since Han's Zhaoyang's wheel-like splendor, Wei court's Nine Splendors' illumination — never could they encompass one ten-thousandth of these.
translations.idiomatic: Not even the splendor of Han's Zhaoyang Hall or the radiance of Wei's Nine Splendors could encompass one ten-thousandth of this.

sentences.zh: 徒以所選止於軍署之內，徵引極乎厮皁之間，非若晉氏採擇濫及冠冕也。

translations.literal: Merely because those selected stopped within military offices' bounds, recruitment and citation reaching only among menials and servants — not like Jin house's selection spreading undiscriminately even to cap-and-girdle families.
translations.idiomatic: At least selection was confined to military compounds and recruits were drawn only from menial ranks — unlike the Jin, whose choices indiscriminately reached even to families of high office.

sentences.zh: [29]且愛止帷房，權無外授，戚屬餼賚，歲時不過肴漿，斯為美矣。

translations.literal: [29] Moreover love stopped within bed-curtains, power not outwardly delegated; kin received seasonal gifts, year-times not exceeding meat broth — this was beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: [29] Moreover, affection was confined to the bedchamber and authority was not extended outward; kin received seasonal gifts of no more than simple food and drink — in this there was beauty.

sentences.zh: 及太祖之傾惑潘嫗，謀及婦人；

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Taizu's being wholly deluded by Lady Pan, plots reaching even to women;
translations.idiomatic: Then came Emperor Wen's infatuation with Lady Pan, when counsel reached even into women's hands;

sentences.zh: 大明之淪溺殷姬，並后匹嫡，至使多難起於肌膚，并命行於同產，又況進於此者乎。

translations.literal: Daming's drowning in Lady Yin, equal empresses matching legitimate wives — to the point of making many calamities rise from skin and flesh, joined lives executed among same birth — how much more what advances beyond this?
translations.idiomatic: and Emperor Xiaowu's obsession with Lady Yin, elevating a consort to rival the empress — until calamities rose from the emperor's own flesh, and brothers of the same womb were put to death together; what of those who went even further?

sentences.zh: 以斯言之，三代、二漢之亡於淫嬖，非不幸也。

translations.literal: By this speaking, the Three Dynasties and the two Han's perishing at licentious favoritism — it was not misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed in this light, the fall of the Three Dynasties and the two Han through licentious indulgence was no accident.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation notes

sentences.zh: 比房 「房」下疑有奪字。

translations.literal: Bi fang ('Equal quarters'): below 'fang' a missing character is suspected.
translations.idiomatic: Bi fang ('Equal quarters'): a character may be missing after 'fang'.

sentences.zh: 臣等請上宋王太后號皇太后 各本並作「臣等參受宋王太后號」，據元龜一八九訂正。

translations.literal: Your ministers request elevating the Princess Dowager of the Prince of Song to the title Empress Dowager: all editions read 'Your ministers received the title of the Princess Dowager of the Prince of Song'; corrected according to Yuan Gui 189.
translations.idiomatic: 'Your ministers request elevating the Princess Dowager of the Prince of Song to the title Empress Dowager': all editions read 'Your ministers received the title of the Princess Dowager of the Prince of Song'; corrected from Yuan Gui, juan 189.

sentences.zh: 妻高密叔孫氏封遷陵永平鄉君 各本並作「封永陵平鄉君」，據南史改。

translations.literal: His wife, née Shusun of Gaomi, was enfeoffed as Lady of Yongping Township in Qianling: all editions read 'Enfeoffed Lady of Ping Township, Yongling'; changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'His wife, née Shusun of Gaomi, was enfeoffed as Lady of Yongping Township in Qianling': all editions read 'Enfeoffed Lady of Ping Township, Yongling'; corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 州郡志郢州武陵太守領遷陵侯相。

translations.literal: The Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies states: the Administrator of Wuling in Ying Province concurrently held the post of Chancellor of the Marquisate of Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: The Treatise on Provinces and Commanderies records that the Administrator of Wuling in Ying Province also served as Chancellor of the Marquisate of Qianling.

sentences.zh: 永平蓋即遷陵縣之鄉名。

translations.literal: Yongping was presumably the name of a township in Qianling County.
translations.idiomatic: Yongping was presumably the name of a township within Qianling County.

sentences.zh: 少帝司馬皇后諱茂英 「皇后」各本並作「皇太妃」，據南史、御覽一四九引改。

translations.literal: Empress Sima, consort of Emperor Shao, personal name Maoying: 'Empress' in all editions reads 'Imperial Consort Dowager'; changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties and Imperial Readings juan 149 citation.
translations.idiomatic: 'Empress Sima, consort of Emperor Shao, personal name Maoying': all editions read 'Imperial Consort Dowager' for 'Empress'; corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties and Imperial Readings, juan 149.

sentences.zh: 時年四十七 張森楷校勘記云：「按少帝死年十九，則妃于時亦當二十左右。

translations.literal: At the time she was forty-seven. Zhang Senkai's collation note says: 「According to Emperor Shao's death at nineteen, the consort at that time should also have been about twenty.
translations.idiomatic: 'She was forty-seven at the time': Zhang Senkai's collation note observes: 「Since Emperor Shao died at nineteen, the consort at that time should have been about twenty.

sentences.zh: 後十六七年至元嘉十六年卒，應年三十六七，不應四十七，疑有誤。」

translations.literal: Sixteen or seventeen years later she died in the sixteenth year of Yuanjia — she should have been thirty-six or thirty-seven, not forty-seven; an error is suspected.」
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen or seventeen years later she died in the sixteenth year of Yuanjia; she should have been thirty-six or thirty-seven, not forty-seven — an error is likely.」

sentences.zh: 武帝胡婕妤諱道安 「道安」各本並作「道女」，據南史、御覽一四二引改。

translations.literal: Lady Hu, Elegant Beauty of Emperor Wu, personal name Dao'an: 'Dao'an' in all editions reads 'Dao'nu'; changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties and Imperial Readings juan 142 citation.
translations.idiomatic: 'Lady Hu, Elegant Beauty of Emperor Wu, personal name Dao'an': all editions read 'Dao'nu' for 'Dao'an'; corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties and Imperial Readings, juan 142.

sentences.zh: 上執手流涕問所欲言 「言」字上，各本並有「不」字，據南史刪。

translations.literal: The emperor, holding her hand, wept and asked what she wished to say: above the character 'speak,' all editions have the character 'not'; deleted according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'The emperor, holding her hand, wept and asked what she wished to say': all editions insert 'not' before 'speak'; removed per the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 房樂昭理 「昭」文選作「韶」。

translations.literal: Chambers' music, orderly and clear: 'Zhao' in the Selections of Refined Literature reads 'Shao'.
translations.idiomatic: 'Chambers' music, orderly and clear': the Selections of Refined Literature has 'Shao' for 'Zhao'.

sentences.zh: 李善注引禮記注曰：「韶，繼也。」

translations.literal: Li Shan's commentary cites the Commentary on the Record of Rites: 「Shao means 'to continue.'」
translations.idiomatic: Li Shan's commentary cites the Record of Rites commentary: 「Shao means 'to continue.'」

sentences.zh: 戒涼在肂 「肂」各本並作「律」，據文選改。

translations.literal: Guarding against chill at the temporary coffin: 'Si' (temporary interment) in all editions reads 'lu'; changed according to the Selections of Refined Literature.
translations.idiomatic: 'Guarding against chill at the temporary coffin': all editions read 'lu' for 'si' (temporary interment); corrected from the Selections of Refined Literature.

sentences.zh: 李善注引儀禮注曰：「死三日而肂，三月而葬。」

translations.literal: Li Shan's commentary cites the Commentary on the Ceremonies and Rites: 「Three days after death comes temporary interment; three months later, burial.」
translations.idiomatic: Li Shan's commentary cites the Ceremonies and Rites commentary: 「Three days after death comes temporary interment; burial follows three months later.」

sentences.zh: 說文曰：「肂，瘞也。」

translations.literal: The Shuowen says: 「Si means 'to inter.'」
translations.idiomatic: The Shuowen states: 「Si means 'to inter.'」

sentences.zh: 沈美人者太祖所幸也 「太祖」各本並作「太宗」。

translations.literal: Beautiful Lady Shen was one favored by Emperor Taizu: 'Taizu' in all editions reads 'Taizong'.
translations.idiomatic: 'Beautiful Lady Shen was one favored by Emperor Taizu': all editions read 'Taizong' for 'Taizu'.

sentences.zh: 按太宗即明帝，沈美人為明帝生母沈婕妤，此太宗當作太祖，今改正。

translations.literal: Note: Taizong is Emperor Ming; Beautiful Lady Shen was his birth mother, Elegant Beauty Shen — here 'Taizong' should be 'Taizu'; corrected now.
translations.idiomatic: Note: 'Taizong' refers to Emperor Ming; Beautiful Lady Shen was the birth mother of Emperor Ming, Elegant Beauty Shen — 'Taizong' should read 'Taizu'; corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 趙蕭臧光祿袁敬公平樂鄉君墓 「鄉君」各本並作「郡君」。

translations.literal: Tomb of the Zhao, Xiao, and Zang Grand Masters, Jinggong Yuan, and the Lady of Pingle Township: 'Township Lady' in all editions reads 'Commandery Lady'.
translations.idiomatic: 'Tomb of the Zhao, Xiao, and Zang Grandees, Jinggong Yuan, and the Lady of Pingle Township': all editions read 'Commandery Lady' for 'Township Lady'.

sentences.zh: 據南史改正。

translations.literal: Corrected according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按上云追贈豫章郡新淦縣平樂鄉君，則此不當稱平樂郡君，疑誤。

translations.literal: Note: above it says she was posthumously granted Lady of Pingle Township in Xingan County, Yuzhang Commandery — here she should not be called Lady of Pingle Commandery; an error is suspected.
translations.idiomatic: Note: the text above records posthumous enfeoffment as Lady of Pingle Township in Xingan County, Yuzhang Commandery — 'Lady of Pingle Commandery' here is likely an error.

sentences.zh: 后父湛自有傳 「湛」各本並作「湛之」，據本傳刪「之」字。

translations.literal: The empress's father Zhan has his own biography: 'Zhan' in all editions reads 'Zhanzhi'; the character 'zhi' deleted according to his biography.
translations.idiomatic: 'The empress's father Zhan has his own biography': all editions read 'Zhanzhi' for 'Zhan'; 'zhi' removed per his biography.

sentences.zh: 徽音克嗣 「克」各本並作「充」，據元龜一八九改。

translations.literal: Virtuous renown able to succeed: 'Ke' in all editions reads 'chong'; changed according to Yuan Gui 189.
translations.idiomatic: 'Virtuous renown able to succeed': all editions read 'chong' for 'ke'; corrected from Yuan Gui, juan 189.

sentences.zh: 謹奉尊號曰皇太后 各本並脫「謹」字，據元龜一八九補。

translations.literal: Respectfully presenting the honored title Empress Dowager: all editions omit the character 'respectfully'; supplemented according to Yuan Gui 189.
translations.idiomatic: 'Respectfully presenting the honored title Empress Dowager': all editions omit 'respectfully'; restored from Yuan Gui, juan 189.

sentences.zh: 太宗盡心祗事 「太宗」各本並作「世祖」。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming devoted himself in reverent service: 'Emperor Ming' in all editions reads 'Emperor Shizu'.
translations.idiomatic: 'Emperor Ming devoted himself in reverent service': all editions read 'Emperor Shizu' for 'Emperor Ming'.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「案文義，當云『太宗盡心祗事』，『世祖』誤。」

translations.literal: Sun Bi's Critical Study of the Book of Song says: 「According to the sense of the text, it should read 'Emperor Ming devoted himself in reverent service'; 'Emperor Shizu' is an error.」
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bi's Critical Study of the Book of Song observes: 「By the sense of the passage, it should read 'Emperor Ming devoted himself in reverent service'; 'Emperor Shizu' is wrong.」

sentences.zh: 按孫說是，今改正。

translations.literal: Note: Sun's view is correct; corrected now.
translations.idiomatic: Sun's view is accepted; corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 尚書嘏之子也 各本並脫「書」字。

translations.literal: He was the son of Minister Gu: all editions omit the character 'shu' (minister).
translations.idiomatic: 'He was the son of Minister Gu': all editions omit 'shu' (minister).

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「當作尚書嘏之子。」

translations.literal: Sun Bi's Critical Study of the Book of Song says: 「It should read 'son of Minister Gu.'」
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bi's Critical Study of the Book of Song says: 「It should read 'son of Minister Gu.'」

sentences.zh: 按孫說是，今補正。

translations.literal: Note: Sun's view is correct; supplemented and corrected now.
translations.idiomatic: Sun's view is accepted; restored and corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 母晉孝武帝女鄱陽公主 張森楷校勘記云：「據晉書王導傳，公主是簡文帝女，孝武帝妹。

translations.literal: His mother was the Princess of Poyang, daughter of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin. Zhang Senkai's collation note says: 「According to the biography of Wang Dao in the History of Jin, the princess was a daughter of Emperor Jianwen and younger sister of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: 'His mother was the Princess of Poyang, daughter of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin': Zhang Senkai's collation note observes: 「According to the biography of Wang Dao in the History of Jin, the princess was a daughter of Emperor Jianwen and younger sister of Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 此女字疑是妹字之誤。」

translations.literal: Here the character 'daughter' is suspected to be an error for 'younger sister.'」
translations.idiomatic: The character 'daughter' here is likely a mistake for 'younger sister.'」

sentences.zh: 當以臨汝公主降嬪 「臨汝公主」各本並作「臨海公主」，據南齊書江斅傳改正。

translations.literal: The Princess of Linru will descend to become my spouse: 'Princess of Linru' in all editions reads 'Princess of Linhai'; corrected according to the biography of Jiang Jiao in the Book of Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: 'The Princess of Linru will descend to become my spouse': all editions read 'Princess of Linhai' for 'Princess of Linru'; corrected from the biography of Jiang Jiao in the Book of Southern Qi.

sentences.zh: 洪頤煊諸史考異云：「按何尚之傳，顒之尚太祖第四女臨海惠公主，封號不應同名。

translations.literal: Hong Yixuan's Comparative Study of Various Histories says: 「According to the biography of He Shangzhi, Yan's wife was the fourth daughter of Emperor Taizu, Princess Hui of Linhai — the enfeoffment titles should not share the same name.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Yixuan's Comparative Study of Various Histories notes: 「According to the biography of He Shangzhi, Yan married Emperor Taizu's fourth daughter, Princess Hui of Linhai — the titles should not be identical.

sentences.zh: 南齊書江斅傳，尚孝武帝女臨汝公主。

translations.literal: The biography of Jiang Jiao in the Book of Southern Qi records marriage to the Princess of Linru, daughter of Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: The biography of Jiang Jiao in the Book of Southern Qi records marriage to Emperor Xiaowu's daughter, the Princess of Linru.

sentences.zh: 『臨海』當是『臨汝』之譌。」

translations.literal: 'Linhai' should be a corruption of 'Linru.'」
translations.idiomatic: 'Linhai' is likely a corruption of 'Linru.'」

sentences.zh: 媒訪莫尋 「媒」各本並作「謀」，據南史改。

translations.literal: Matchmakers sought but none found: 'Mei' (matchmaker) in all editions reads 'mou' (to seek); changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'Matchmakers sought but none found': all editions read 'mou' (to seek) for 'mei' (matchmaker); corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 謝莊殆自同於矇叟 「矇叟」各本並作「矇室」，據南史改。

translations.literal: Xie Zhuang was nearly like a blind old man himself: 'Meng sou' (blind old man) in all editions reads 'meng shi'; changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'Xie Zhuang was nearly like a blind old man himself': all editions read 'meng shi' for 'meng sou' (blind old man); corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 錢大昕廿二史考異云：「案謝莊傳，無尚主事，疑以目疾辭，遂停尚主也。」

translations.literal: Qian Daxin's Comparative Study of the Twenty-Two Histories says: 「According to the biography of Xie Zhuang, there is no record of marrying an imperial princess; it is suspected he declined on account of eye disease and thus ceased the imperial marriage.」
translations.idiomatic: Qian Daxin's Comparative Study of the Twenty-Two Histories observes: 「The biography of Xie Zhuang records no imperial marriage; he likely declined on account of eye disease and the marriage was abandoned.」

sentences.zh: 彼數人者 各本並脫「彼」字，據南史補。

translations.literal: Those several men: all editions omit the character 'bi' (those); supplemented according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'Those several men': all editions omit 'those'; restored from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 咸成恩假 「成」各本並作「有」，據南史、初學記一０引、藝文類聚一六引、御覽一五三引改。

translations.literal: All became favor by marriage connection: 'Cheng' (became) in all editions reads 'you' (have); changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties, Initial Learning Notes juan 10 citation, Literary Anthology juan 16 citation, and Imperial Readings juan 153 citation.
translations.idiomatic: 'All became favor by marriage connection': all editions read 'have' for 'became'; corrected from the History of Southern Dynasties, Initial Learning Notes juan 10, Literary Anthology juan 16, and Imperial Readings juan 153.

sentences.zh: 至衞將軍 「衞將軍」南史作「右衞將軍」。

translations.literal: Reached Guard General: 'Guard General' in the History of Southern Dynasties reads 'Right Guard General'.
translations.idiomatic: 'Reached Guard General': the History of Southern Dynasties has 'Right Guard General' for 'Guard General'.

sentences.zh: 亮收斬之 各本並作「收亮斬之」，孫虨宋書考論云：「案文義當為『亮收斬之』。」

translations.literal: Liang captured and beheaded him: all editions read 'captured Liang and beheaded him'; Sun Bi's Critical Study of the Book of Song says: 「According to the sense of the text, it should read 'Liang captured and beheaded him.'」
translations.idiomatic: 'Liang captured and beheaded him': all editions read 'captured Liang and beheaded him'; Sun Bi's Critical Study of the Book of Song observes: 「By the sense of the passage, it should read 'Liang captured and beheaded him.'」

sentences.zh: 按孫說是，今改正。

translations.literal: Note: Sun's view is correct; corrected now.
translations.idiomatic: Sun's view is accepted; corrected accordingly.

sentences.zh: 文帝沈婕妤諱容姬 各本並脫「姬」字，據南史補。

translations.literal: Lady Shen, Elegant Beauty of Emperor Wen, personal name Rongji: all editions omit the character 'ji'; supplemented according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'Lady Shen, Elegant Beauty of Emperor Wen, personal name Rongji': all editions omit 'ji'; restored from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 太宗改封又為湘東王妃 各本並脫「又為」二字，據南史補。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming's title was changed, she again became Princess Consort of Xiangdong: all editions omit the two characters 'again became'; supplemented according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'When Emperor Ming's title was changed, she again became Princess Consort of Xiangdong': all editions omit 'again became'; restored from the History of Southern Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 按太宗即明帝，初封淮陽王，元嘉二十九年，改封湘東王，故其妃亦改稱湘東王妃。

translations.literal: Note: Taizong is Emperor Ming; initially enfeoffed Prince of Huaiyang, in the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia changed to Prince of Xiangdong — hence his consort's title also changed to Princess Consort of Xiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Note: 'Taizong' is Emperor Ming; he was first enfeoffed Prince of Huaiyang and in the twenty-ninth year of Yuanjia was re-enfeoffed Prince of Xiangdong — hence his consort's title was likewise changed to Princess Consort of Xiangdong.

sentences.zh: 改諸國太妃曰太妃

translations.literal: Changed the grand consorts of all princedoms to the title Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: The title of the grand consorts of all princedoms was changed to Grand Consort.

sentences.zh: 〈妃音怡〉

translations.literal: 〈Fei is pronounced yi.〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Fei is pronounced yi.〉

sentences.zh: 「太妃」南史、御覽一四二引作「太姬」。

translations.literal: 'Grand Consort' in the History of Southern Dynasties and Imperial Readings juan 142 citation reads 'Grand Lady'.
translations.idiomatic: 'Grand Consort' appears as 'Grand Lady' in the History of Southern Dynasties and Imperial Readings, juan 142.

sentences.zh: 孫虨宋書考論云：「姬字是。」

translations.literal: Sun Bi's Critical Study of the Book of Song says: 「The character 'ji' is correct.」
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bi's Critical Study of the Book of Song holds: 「The character 'ji' is correct.」

sentences.zh: 飲食男女人之大欲存焉 「人」各本並作「民」，據禮記禮運原文改正。

translations.literal: Food, drink, male and female — in these man's great desires reside: 'man' in all editions reads 'common people'; corrected according to the original text of the Evolution of Rites in the Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: 'Food, drink, male and female — in these man's great desires reside': all editions read 'common people' for 'man'; corrected from the original text of the Record of Rites, Evolution of Rites.

sentences.zh: 非若晉氏採擇濫及冠冕也 各本並脫「若」字，據南史補。

translations.literal: Not like the Jin house's selection spreading undiscriminately even to cap-and-girdle families: all editions omit the character 'like'; supplemented according to the History of Southern Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: 'Not like the Jin house's selection spreading undiscriminately even to cap-and-girdle families': all editions omit 'like'; restored from the History of Southern Dynasties.
